Genome-wide ChIP-seq studies demonstrated colocalization of endogenous HNF-1{beta} and the core NuRD subunits GATAD2A, CHD4, and MBD3 at 2,776 primarily intergenic and intronic sites in native chromatin from wild-type renal epithelial cells. NuRD co-occupancy at 628 of the sites (22.6%) was reduced in the absence of HNF-1{beta}. Of the 628 HNF-1{beta}-dependent NuRD-occupied sites, 113 sites (18.2%) showed higher ATAC-seq peaks, indicative of open chromatin, and enrichment of histone H3 lysine-27 (H3K27) acetylation, indicative of active enhancers, in wild-type cells compared to HNF-1{beta}-deficient cells. Correlation with transcriptomic profiles in wild-type and HNF-1{beta}-deficient cells revealed that most of the sites were located near genes that are activated by HNF-1{beta}. Knockdown of CHD4 with shRNA resulted in decreased expression of 67 HNF-1{beta}-regulated genes that contained nearby NuRD and HNF-1{beta} co-occupied sites. Collectively, these results demonstrate that HNF-1{beta} recruits the NuRD complex resulting in H3K27 acetylation and chromatin opening and leading to gene activation. Our findings reveal a new mechanism of HNF-1{beta}-dependent gene expression and expand the role of the NuRD complex in gene activation at distal enhancers.

items.title_en: Excluded Volume Effect-induced Shrinkage for Resolution Enhancement of Hydrogel Bioconstructs
items.title_zh: 排除体积效应诱导的收缩用于增强水凝胶生物构建体的分辨率
items.abstract_en: Biofabrication of hydrogel materials is usually constrained by process-specific resolution limits. Here, we introduce excluded volume effect-induced shrinkage (EVER), a dehydration-enabled resolution enhancement strategy that achieves dimensional refinement via post-processing. In this approach, we treat biofabricated constructs with hydrophilic macromolecular crowding agent bath, with poloxamer as a representative. With EVER treatment, gelatin-based constructs can reach a dimension reduction of up to ~49% with an estimated volumetric reduction of ~87%. Shape fidelity was well retained after shrinkage across different constructs and could be stabilized by introducing secondary crosslinking. In extrusion bioprinted cell-laden constructs, myoblasts retained a considerable cell viability right after the shrinkage treatment and recovered significantly by day 1, with subsequent cell spreading and increasing proliferation over 7 days. Without the need of continued immersion in the shrinkage bath, EVER provides a hardware-independent route for refining hydrogel structures while retaining encapsulated cell compatibility.

items.title_en: MPFIL: Multi-Level Protein Feature Integration for Predicting Mutation-Induced Protein-Protein Binding Affinity Changes
items.title_zh: MPFIL：多层级蛋白质特征整合用于预测突变诱导的蛋白质-蛋白质结合亲和力变化
items.abstract_en: Predicting mutation-induced changes in protein protein binding affinity ({triangleup}{triangleup}G) is challenging because mutations can affect both local residue environments and the structural organization of protein complexes. Existing approaches often rely on handcrafted physicochemical, energetic, or evolutionary features, which introduce additional computational costs and require domain-specific knowledge. In this work, we propose MPFIL, a multi-level protein feature integration framework for predicting mutation-induced protein-protein binding affin ity changes. MPFIL integrates structural and sequential infor mation to characterize mutation effects from complementary perspectives. Its structural feature extraction module captures mutation-induced structural changes and differential information between wild-type and mutant complexes, while sequence feature extraction modules model local residue context and long-range dependencies. The resulting features are integrated for {triangleup}{triangleup}G prediction. We evaluate MPFIL on three benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate competitive and consistent performance across different protein complex settings, while ablation studies verify the contribution of the structural and sequential features. These results support the effectiveness of multi-level protein feature integration for modeling mutation induced changes in protein-protein binding affinity.

items.title_en: NMR-measured Per-residue Electrostatic Potentials Reveal the Importance of Arginine-Lysine Balance on the Conformational Ensemble of Disordered Histone H3 Tails in Nucleosome Core Particles
items.title_zh: NMR测量的逐残基静电势揭示精氨酸-赖氨酸平衡对核小体核心颗粒中无序组蛋白H3尾部构象系综的重要性
items.abstract_en: Biophysical studies of chromatin have provided key insights into how the genome is regulated. Many atomic resolution structures of the fundamental building block of chromatin, the nucleosome core particle (NCP), as well as larger NCP arrays, both in isolation and in complex with effectors, or with post-translational modifications, have been elucidated. These provide in-depth pictures of key functional interactions. Considerably less information is available on the intrinsically disordered nucleosome tails that are critically important for higher order interactions in chromatin, and for transcription, DNA repair, and phase separation, and that serve as hubs for post-translational modifications. Here we focus on the tail of one of the four histones, histone-3 (H3), and measure electrostatic potentials at each of its amide proton positions in isolated NCPs via solution NMR spectroscopy. Using these potentials, in concert with molecular dynamics simulations, an ensemble of structures is calculated for WT H3 tails, as well as variants where all tail arginines are replaced by lysines (R2K) or vice versa (K2R). Our ensembles reveal that K2R tails have a higher propensity to occupy the most negatively charged region of the NCP between the DNA gyres than R2K or WT tails, while lysine enriched tails have an increased relative preference for the less negative regions near the DNA entry and exit points. The structural ensembles provide insight into differences in interactions between neighboring particles that lead to changes in diffusion and phase separation propensities between the NCP variants.

items.title_en: Cancer cells acquire cysteine directly from a reduced tumor microenvironment
items.title_zh: 癌细胞直接从还原性肿瘤微环境中获取半胱氨酸
items.abstract_en: The metabolic environment of a tumor is shaped by the nutrients available in its interstitial fluid, yet the redox composition of that fluid is poorly defined. Measuring sulfur metabolites in the interstitial fluid of tumors, matched healthy organs, and serum across three mouse models of cancer, we find that the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a chemically reduced compartment in which free cysteine predominates over its oxidized form, cystine. This is especially pronounced in the lung TME, where cystine is nearly absent. We further show that lung cancer cells take up cysteine and cystine with comparable efficiency and proliferate on cysteine alone, and that the abundant glutathione in the TME helps keep cysteine reduced through disulfide exchange. In a medium formulated to match the sulfur composition of the lung tumor interstitial fluid, cells become independent of cystine import through xCT. Cells cultured in this medium were resistant to glutaminase inhibitors, oxidants and ferroptosis inducers, and better maintained NADPH levels under oxidative challenge. These findings suggest that standard culture conditions overestimate the dependence of cancer cells on cystine uptake and their vulnerability to oxidative stress-targeting therapies.

items.title_en: Fine-tuning an intracellular allosteric pocket programs GPCR signaling bias
items.title_zh: 精细调控细胞内变构口袋可编程GPCR信号偏倚
items.abstract_en: Biased signaling of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers a route for precise therapeutics with fewer adverse effects. Intracellular allosteric ligands can impose such bias, yet how subtle chemical changes within these pockets reshape receptor-transducer coupling and downstream signaling remains unclear. Here, we systematically fine-tuned the intracellular allosteric pocket of neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) through chemical modification of the {beta}-arrestin-biased ligand SBI-553. Minor changes to the ligand scaffold altered transducer-coupling preferences, generating distinct profiles of G-protein and {beta}-arrestin signaling. Cryo-electron microscopy structures of NTSR1-{beta}-arrestin2 complexes bound to designed allosteric probes revealed ligand-dependent remodeling of the intracellular cavity that reshapes the receptor-effector interface. Alanine scanning identified transducer-sensitive residues within and beyond the immediate ligand-contact region. In mice, SBI-553 and N065 produced distinct physiological profiles, with N065 improving survival in a lethal endotoxemia model. Finally, phosphoproteomic profiling revealed partially overlapping but distinct downstream signaling profiles among the three modulators. Together, these findings establish the intracellular allosteric pocket as a tunable determinant of transducer coupling and show that closely related modulators can generate distinct signaling and physiological profiles.

items.title_en: Modulation of planarian seizure-like activity via antiseizure medications
items.title_zh: 通过抗癫痫药物调节涡虫的癫痫样活动
items.abstract_en: Acute chemical exposure to organophosphorus compounds (OPs) arising from terrorist attacks or accidental poisonings pose a serious threat to human health. Acetylcholinesterase inhibition due to acute OP exposure causes a cholinergic crisis, manifested as increased secretions, respiratory distress, loss of consciousness, seizures, and ultimately death if left untreated. Benzodiazepines, such as midazolam, are currently used to stop OP-induced seizures, but must be administered within minutes after exposure to be effective. This makes midazolam impractical for large-scale civilian emergencies. Thus, there is a need to identify novel antiseizure medications (ASMs) that are equally effective even when administered later. It has been challenging to identify such compounds with traditional mammalian testing; high throughput screening assays that can quickly and cost-effectively evaluate many candidates for their potential as an ASM are needed. Planarians are aquatic invertebrates that are suitable organismal models for OP neurotoxicity studies due to the conservation of OP targets and their ability to metabolize OPs. Here, we built on our prior work that introduced a computational image analysis pipeline to quantify planarian seizure-like activity (pSLA) in two planarian species (Dugesia japonica and Girardia dorotocephala). We previously used this approach to characterize pSLA following acute exposure (up to 30 minutes) to seizurogenic compounds. In the present study, we asked whether pSLA induced by the OP pesticide parathion, pentylenetetrazole, or NMDA could be rescued by co-exposure to four ASMs: midazolam, topiramate, MK-801, and carbamazepine. All tested ASMs were effective at reducing parathion-induced pSLA in one planarian species. However, ASM responses varied substantially across proconvulsants and planarian species. Defining the molecular mechanisms underlying pSLA will be essential for establishing planarians as a reliable model for ASM discovery.

items.title_en: A pump-leak model of epithelia reveals the roles of paracellular pathways in water transport & the importance of boundary conditions
items.abstract_en: We develop a pump-leak model of epithelial transport, where the flux of water through the epithelium is modeled as a compartment, or sink, whose volume grows linearly with time. A method is described for calculating the voltage in the sink compartment, as well as analytical solutions to the system of equations. We show how growing boundary conditions can be used to model a scenario where water and ion fluxes are possible in the steady state. It is possible to drive a continuous flux of water through an epithelium that is powered by the Na+ pump establishing small osmotic gradients between compartments. We show that paracellular pathways play a crucial role in the operation of epithelial transport by ensuring that the flux through the epithelium is electroneutral. For the Na+ pump situated on the basolateral membrane, water fluxes can be directed in the same direction as the Na+ ion by having a high Na+ conductance on the apical membrane and high K+ conductance on the basolateral membrane. Flipping these conductances changes the direction of water fluxes. We introduce a graphic formalism that makes clear the precise mechanism of water transfer, showing the osmotic and electrical constraints. We demonstrate that it is possible when the extracellular osmolarity is low (~10mOsm) for the intracellular osmolarity to exceed that of the former considerably and produce a hyperosmolar solution.

items.title_en: Human prion proteins and mutants through the lens of systems biology
items.abstract_en: Autocatalytic conformational changes of cellular prion proteins (PrPC) to the {beta}-sheet-enriched scrapie isoform (PrPSC) drive prion diseases, yet the precise molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To address this, we employ a multi-pronged framework integrating network-theoretic analyses, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and experimental validation to characterize critical residues governing human PrP (huPrP) structural integrity. Residue Interaction Networks (RINs) of: (A) wild-type (WT) huPrP, and, (B) five disease-associated point mutants (Met166Val, Glu220Lys, Glu200Lys, Asp178Asn, and Ser170Asn) were evaluated using three rigorous network methods: centrality measures, Shortest Path Alteration Fraction (SPAF), and Differential Networks (DN). Across all the diverse point mutations, five residues (Met206, Val209, Val210, Met213, and Cys214) consistently exhibit high centrality scores. SPAF and DN analyses demonstrate that alterations at these positions disrupt connectivity and increase the propensity for misfolding and protease resistance. To validate these topological findings, key residues within the C-terminal domain (121-230) were substituted via site-directed mutagenesis. Thermal denaturation monitored by circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy reveals that the Met213Ala substitution significantly lowers the melting temperature, Tm, relative to the WT, whereas the Val210Ala variant unfolds with a Tm comparable to the WT. Furthermore, MD simulations of de novo AlphaFold-predicted mutant structures corroborate these findings. Mutants exhibit greater structural flexibility and deviation, with average root Mean Square Deviations rising from 0.18 nm (WT) to 0.32 nm (Cys214Ala), 0.29 nm (Met206Ala), and 0.25 nm (Val210Lys). This integration of theoretical and experimental techniques provides a robust framework for identifying critical determinants of protein stability.

items.title_en: Wasting is essential: cachexia is driven by a wound-healing adaptation
items.abstract_en: Background: Several explanations have been given for why cachexia occurs in the presence of severe acute wounds and chronic diseases. None of these explanations address the scope of clinical settings in which cachexia has been observed, nor do they account for the failure of nutritional support to reverse cachexia. We hypothesize that induced muscle wasting (IMW) is an adaptation to support wound healing, and when a wound does not heal, prolonged IMW leads to cachexia. Methods: To evaluate this hypothesis, we developed a mathematical model of IMW. In this model, we compared the time needed for wound healing when IMW was present and when it was inhibited. We also measured the relationship between the pathogen growth rate and final patient muscle mass for chronic diseases such as cancer and tuberculosis, demonstrating the onset of cachexia. Finally, we simulated the effects of nutritional support and contrasted the outcomes of when IMW was present and when it was inhibited. Results: Acute wound healing was ~2-6 times longer without IMW than with IMW. For chronic wounds, steady-state muscle mass strongly depended on the growth rate of the pathogenic agent. Inhibiting IMW was more effective at preventing acute muscle mass loss than nutritional support, and the benefit of nutritional support was enhanced by inhibiting IMW. Nutritional support also increased the speed of healing acute wounds when IMW was inhibited. For cancer with high growth rate, giving nutritional support alone had a negligible effect on steady-state muscle mass. But when IMW was inhibited, muscle mass loss was attenuated. With IMW inhibition, nutritional support with the normal diet was able to abrogate muscle mass loss entirely. Conclusions: Inhibiting IMW slows the healing of acute wounds, supporting our hypothesis that IMW is an adaptation to support rapid wound healing. Our experiments demonstrate that nutritional support is insufficient to prevent severe muscle mass loss while IMW continues. But when IMW is inhibited, nutritional support restores normal levels of muscle mass for both acute and chronic wounds, as well as increasing the rate of wound healing. Discovering and developing methods to inhibit IMW for clinical use will be essential to restore patient muscle mass, ease suffering, and reduce mortality.

items.title_en: Gene-gene and Gene-Environment Interactions Improve Genetic Risk Predictions for Complex Diseases
items.abstract_en: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) assume additive SNP effects, yet genetic risk also arises from interactions between loci and environmental factors that contribute to broad-sense heritability. We developed an extended PRS (ePRS) framework for type 2 diabetes (T2D) that incorporates locus-by-locus non-additive effects beyond those captured by additive single-locus PRS or linkage disequilibrium (LD) tagging. These were modelled as interaction-informed cumulative burden (G+G; summed allele counts), epistasis-screened (GxG; allele count products), and gene-environment effects derived from cardiometabolic variables in electronic health records. Across 235,000 UK Biobank participants, five complementary ePRS models captured largely non-overlapping high-risk individuals, suggesting that a key to individual risk predictions comprises the inclusion of multiple interaction-driven biological components rather than a single signal. A composite score was predictive over traditional additive PRS and predictive of T2D among individuals whose clinical symptoms fall within normal ranges.

items.title_en: A Unified Flexible Large Polysomnography Model for Sleep Staging and Downstream Clinical Screening
items.abstract_en: Polysomnography (PSG) is central to sleep medicine, yet its analysis remains hindered by labor-intensive manual scoring and limited cross-center generalizability. We present LPSGM, a large-scale PSG model trained on 220,500 hours of data from 16 public datasets (24,000 recordings) that addresses two challenges: cross-center sleep staging generalization and PSG-based screening of narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and depression. LPSGM integrates domain-adaptive pre-training, flexible channel configurations, and a unified architecture to accommodate heterogeneous recording protocols. In prospective validation, LPSGM achieves expert-level sleep staging ({kappa} = 0.845 {+/-} 0.066 vs. inter-expert {kappa} = 0.850 {+/-} 0.102) and matches fully supervised models on independent private cohorts. For downstream screening, LPSGM achieves 84.2% accuracy ({kappa} = 0.761) in three-class narcolepsy classification, with cross-institutional transfer for normal-versus-abnormal hypersomnia yielding an AUC of 0.879. Severe OSA screening reaches an AUC of 0.874 without access to respiratory signals. Depression symptom screening achieves an AUC of 0.801 in a surrogate-labeled APPLES cohort, and cross-dataset transfer to an independent clinically diagnosed cohort reaches an AUC of 0.965. These results suggest that LPSGM's pre-trained representations capture sleep-related signatures that generalize across institutions and support PSG-based screening of clinically relevant conditions. The code and pre-trained model are publicly available at https://github.com/Deng-GuiFeng/LPSGM.

items.title_en: Familial factors inflate the estimated effects of genetic liability to ADHD on behavioural outcomes
items.abstract_en: Background: People with ADHD have worse health, behavioural and social outcomes, widely interpreted as evidence that ADHD causes these harms, justifying early identification and treatment. But ADHD clusters in families, and conventional studies cannot separate the effect of a person's own ADHD from the family environment in which it arises. We used a family-based genetic design to distinguish the two. Methods: We used up to 22 genome-wide significant variants associated with ADHD (38,691 cases, 186,843 controls) to estimate effects of genetic liability to ADHD on 16 health and behavioural outcomes. We compared population-based estimates with family-based estimates from within-sibship analyses of up to 164,220 siblings. We tested for heterogeneity between the designs, and applied sensitivity analyses. We involved individuals with lived experience of ADHD in interpreting the findings and shaping how the clinical/public-health implications were described. Findings: Population-based analyses implied that greater genetic liability to ADHD increased smoking, alcohol use and depressive symptoms, and reduced educational attainment, age at first child and cognitive performance. In family-based analyses, these effects attenuated. For example, the effect on number of depressive symptoms fell from 0.059 SD (95% CI 0.039, 0.080) to 0.002 SD (-0.052, 0.055), and age at first child increased from -0.045 SD (-0.058, -0.033) to 0.003 SD (-0.040, 0.047), with significant differences between designs (p=0.048 and p=0.034). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Interpretation: Much of the excess health and behavioural burden attributed to ADHD may reflect the family and environmental context in which ADHD occurs, rather than an individual's own ADHD. Interventions targeting the individual might not reduce these outcomes as much as expected. Distinguishing such effects requires family-based designs. Funding: Medical Research Council, UK Research and Innovation, Research Council of Norway, US National Institute of Mental Health, and Australian National Health and Medical Research Council.

items.title_en: Clinical Significance and Distribution of Cerebrospinal Fluid Type IV Oligoclonal Band Pattern in Neurological Disorders: A Retrospective Analysis
items.abstract_en: Background and Objectives: To characterize the clinical features and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings of patients exhibiting a type IV oligoclonal band (OCB) pattern, defined by the presence of identical IgG bands in both CSF and serum. Methods: This retrospective observational study included all consecutive adult patients with a type IV pattern detected during routine CSF analysis at Geneva University Hospitals in 2023. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected through chart review. Results: A total of 178 patients were included. The mean age was 60.2 years (SD 16.5), and 51.7% were female. The type IV pattern was most frequently observed in non-inflammatory neurological diseases (NIND) (n=103, 57.9%). Other inflammatory neurological diseases accounted for 37 cases (20.7%), multiple sclerosis was identified in 8 patients (4.5%), and peripheral nervous system disorders were present in 20 patients (11.2%). Systemic inflammatory comorbidities were observed in 40 patients (22.5%). An elevated albumin quotient was present in 73 patients (41%) and was most common among those with CNS infections, aseptic meningitis, CNS neoplastic diseases, and peripheral nervous system disorder. Repeated CSF analyses demonstrated temporal fluctuations in the type IV pattern in some patients, without corresponding changes in diagnosis. Discussion: The type IV pattern is predominantly associated with NIND and is relatively uncommon in multiple sclerosis. Although it may reflect systemic immune activation and/or blood brain barrier dysfunction in certain inflammatory conditions, its clinical significance remains nonspecific. These findings support cautious interpretation of the type IV pattern in routine clinical practice.

items.title_en: Educational expectations and needs of individuals scheduled for breast surgery within the Primary Nursing Model: a qualitative study
items.abstract_en: Background. A diagnosis of breast cancer may represent a potentially destabilizing event, with significant physical, psychological, and social implications. Individuals scheduled for breast surgery require clear, understandable, and personalized information to prepare for surgery and manage the postoperative period. However, a discrepancy may arise between perceived informational needs and the information actually received. The Primary Nursing model, based on continuity of care and the presence of a designated primary nurse, may promote greater personalization of nurse-led patient education. Aim. To explore the experiences of individuals scheduled for breast surgery in relation to the nurse-led patient education received throughout the perioperative pathway, in order to understand their educational expectations, informational needs, and perceptions of the usefulness of the educational interventions provided within the Primary Nursing model. Design. A qualitative study with a phenomenological orientation. Methods. The study will be conducted at the European Institute of Oncology. Participants will be recruited through convenience sampling among individuals diagnosed with breast cancer who have undergone surgery and received the nurse-led discharge education routinely provided. Approximately 20 participants are expected to be enrolled; the final sample size will be determined according to the principle of data saturation. Data will be collected through semi-structured interviews conducted approximately two weeks after discharge by a member of the research team who is not involved in the participants Clinical care. The interviews, lasting approximately 30-40 minutes, will be audio-recorded with prior consent, transcribed verbatim, and assigned a sequential identification code. Sociodemographic data and clinical information extracted from the medical records will also be collected. The transcripts will be analyzed using thematic analysis according to Braun and Clarke, with a phenomenological orientation. Expected contribution. The study may contribute to understanding potential discrepancies between educational expectations, informational needs, and the perceived usefulness of the information received, thereby informing clinical practice toward personalized educational interventions consistent with continuity of care.

items.title_en: Statistical Analysis Plan for the REDEP study: Effectiveness of dual-mobility cups for preventing dislocation after primary total hip arthroplasty by a posterolateral approach compared to unipolar cups in elderly patients
items.abstract_en: Periprosthetic hip dislocation is a frequent complication after primary total hip arthroplasty. Observational studies suggest that dual mobility cups may reduce dislocation risk to approximately 1%, but definitive randomized evidence supporting their routine use in primary total hip arthroplasty is absent. The REDEP trial is the first prospective, randomized controlled trial that compares dual mobility cups with unipolar cups in patients [≥]70 years who electively undergo primary total hip arthroplasty via a posterolateral approach. The primary objective of the trial is to determine the difference in the number of patients who suffer a periprosthetic dislocation of the hip within 1 year after primary total hip arthroplasty in this population. Other outcomes include the difference in the total number of hip dislocations (including recurrent dislocations within patients), differences in patient-reported outcome measures, and differences in the incidence of (serious) adverse events. This statistical analysis plan describes the primary statistical analysis for the REDEP study. The analyses described herein were defined prior to database lock and unblinding. Secondary analyses will be described in subsequent versions of this statistical analysis plan.

items.title_en: Implementation of high-dose glucocorticoids and opioid consumption in the first 24 hours after elective hip and knee arthroplasty: a natural experiment study of 47,317 procedures in Eastern Denmark
items.abstract_en: Background: In Denmark, high-dose perioperative glucocorticoids were implemented stepwise for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA), total knee arthroplasty (TKA), and unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA). We aimed to estimate the opioid-sparing effect of adding a single high dose of glucocorticoids to the analgesic regimen. Methods: In this prespecified analysis of a multicentre natural experiment using electronic health record data, we included all elective THA, TKA, or UKA procedures performed in Eastern Denmark from 2017-2025, with no exclusion criteria. At each centre, procedures before implementation of high-dose glucocorticoids served as controls, whereas procedures after implementation comprised the intervention group. A high dose was defined as [≥]16 mg or 0.2 mg/kg dexamethasone or [≥]80 mg methylprednisolone. The primary outcome was the adjusted between-group difference in 0-24h opioid consumption. The minimal important difference was 5 mg IV morphine equivalents. Secondary outcomes were maximum 0-10 numerical rating scale (NRS) pain score, incidence of opioid-related adverse events, hospital length of stay, and days alive and out of hospital at 30 days. Results: We analysed 47,317 procedures performed at nine centres: 13,010 controls and 34,307 in the intervention group. During the study period, five of nine centres implemented high-dose glucocorticoids for THA patients, two of eight for TKA/UKA patients. High-dose glucocorticoids were administered to 6% and 92% of patients before and after implementation, respectively. The implementation was associated with an adjusted mean reduction of 3.8 mg IV morphine equivalents (95% CI 3.3 to 4.3) and a 0.8-point lower maximum recorded pain score (99% CI 0.7 to 0.9) in the first 24 hours, with no statistically significant differences in the remaining outcomes. Conclusions: Implementation of high-dose glucocorticoids was associated with only a small drop in opioid consumption, below the minimal important difference. Online registration: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.11.25339982

items.title_en: CREBBP variants underlying Menke-Hennekam syndrome exhibit histone acetyltransferase hyperactivity with divergent phase behaviors
items.abstract_en: Menke-Hennekam syndrome (MKHK) is a neurodevelopmental disease characterized by specific pathogenic regions within the transcriptional coactivator CREB-binding protein (CREBBP). CREBBP regulates gene expression through histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity and involves IDR-dependent transcriptional condensates. Although domain-specific phenotypes and distinct DNA methylation episignatures have been recognized in MKHK, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain widely unclear. In this study, we identified a recurrent missense variant, p.(R1868W) [R1868W]) and a novel splice variant r.5963_5969del,p.(Cys1723Thrfs*19) [C1723fs] in two families clinically diagnosed with MKHK and manifesting developmental delay, characteristic facial features, and growth impairment. R1868W and C1723fs exhibited increased auto-, nonhistone protein, and histone acetylation. Despite these shared enzymatic abnormalities, the variants promoted divergent disruption in liquid-liquid phase separation. The recurrent CBP-ID4 variant R1868W activated the formation of low-mobility aberrant nuclear condensates, whereas the C-terminal, truncating variant C1723fs, impaired condensate formation and showed diffuse nuclear localization. Treatment with the selective p300/CBP HAT inhibitor A485 partially restored condensate dynamics and fusion-relaxation behavior in R1868W. Furthermore, R1868W recruited BRD4 around condensates in an acetylation-dependent manner, which was suppressed by the BET inhibitor JQ1. Together, these findings suggest that aberrant condensate material properties arising from disrupted CREBBP IDR-dependent regulation play a critical role in the molecular pathogenesis of MKHK.

items.title_en: Comparing the Phenotypic and Genetic Differences Between Autistic Regression and Autism Without Regression Using the SPARK Cohort
items.abstract_en: The biology of autistic regression (Autreg) remains poorly understood. We investigated Autreg's phenotypic and genetic landscape in 51 633 individuals from the SPARK cohort. We calculated the frequencies of parental-reported language regression and regression affecting social, play, toileting, and/or other developmental domains, and ages at skill regression and regain within SPARK. We compared developmental milestones, quantitative developmental measures, and selected other phenotypes in Autreg and autism without regression (Autnreg). Rare damaging coding variants and polygenic scores (PGS) in Autreg and Autnreg were compared using genome sequencing data. Rare variants were analyzed using the Transmission And De novo Association (TADA) framework in 1 107 Autreg and 974 Autnreg individuals, followed by pathway enrichment analysis. PGS for autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, epilepsy, and schizophrenia were initially compared. PGS validation was conducted in 14 001 Autnreg and 11 638 Autreg individuals using larger SPARK genotyping data. We identified regression in 43% of autistic individuals. Other regression occurred later than language regression, and 60% of skill regain occurred within two years. Autreg was associated with lower Vineland-3 Adaptive Behavior Composite scores (p twofold increased odds of epilepsy and intellectual disability (p<0.001). Developmental milestones and quantitative measures had modest differences. TADA analysis highlighted genes involved in nucleotide catabolism, transcription, and focal adhesion, with PTEN emerging as a strong candidate for Autreg. Schizophrenia PGS explained 0.087% of variance in liability to regression among autistic individuals. In conclusion, Autreg was associated with increased neurodevelopmental morbidity. Schizophrenia PGS and rare variants explained a minimal fraction of its etiology.

items.title_en: Cross-Sectional Study of Periodontal Oral Dental Foci of Infection (PODFI) in Medically Compromised Patients at Lille University Hospital
items.abstract_en: Oral dental foci of infection (ODFI), particularly those of periodontal origin, can trigger systemic inflammatory responses that may cause bacteraemia for medically compromised patients. Although guidelines recommend detection and elimination of these foci, precise data on the distribution of periodontal oral dental foci of infection (PODFI) risk within these populations remain scarce. This study aimed to describe periodontal sources of infection in medically compromised patients using a periodontal examination and follow-up form and a recently developed PODFI risk levels classification. This observational, retrospective, cross-sectional, single-center study evaluated medically compromised patients with periodontitis in the dental surgery department of the Lille University Hospital between September 2024 and September 2025. Periodontitis was diagnosed according to the 2017 Classification of Periodontal Diseases established at the 2017 World Workshop. The primary outcome was the distribution of PODFI risk levels (moderate, high, very high). Secondary outcomes aimed to describe periodontal conditions in a specific population of medically compromised patients. Thirty-nine patients were included in this study. Evaluation of PODFI risk (n = 34) revealed a predominance of moderate-risk profiles (67.6 %) and a significant proportion of high-risk profiles (32.4 %); no low-risk or very high-risk profiles were observed. Generalized periodontal inflammation was very common (92 %), with a median of 26 bleeding on probing (BOP) sites and 71 plaque-positive sites, showing a positive correlation (R = 0.52, p = 0.002). Severe and active forms of periodontitis predominated (n = 39), with 74.4 % of cases classified as stage III (28.2 %) or stage IV (46.2 %), and grade B was the most common (56.4 %), followed by grade C (38.5 %) (p = 0.025). Medically compromised patients have a high prevalence of severe and active periodontitis, with nearly one-third of them classified as being at high risk for infection. The recently developed periodontal oral dental foci of infection (PODFI) classification provides a structured and clinically relevant tool for stratifying infection risk and guiding treatment decisions. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm the validity of these PODFI risk levels.

items.title_en: Between- and Within-Person Coupling of Nocturnal Heart Rate and Glucose: Retrospective, Real-World Observational Study of 105,196 Nights From 2648 Adults Using Ultrahuman Ring and Continuous Glucose Monitoring
items.abstract_en: Background: Higher resting or sleeping heart rate (HR) has been associated with poorer glucose metabolism in adults without diabetes. However, these associations were estimated across individuals, and within-person characterization of this co-regulation during naturalistic sleep in large free-living cohorts remains limited. Objective: This study aimed to determine whether average sleeping HR, an indirect index of cardiac autonomic tone, is associated with nocturnal glucose within a participant and between participants, and whether night-to-night irregularity in sleep duration, sleep onset, and wake time is associated with nocturnal glycemia. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, adults who concurrently wore an Ultrahuman Ring and a continuous glucose monitor between January 2024 and June 2025 were analyzed. After participant- and night-level filtering, the cohort comprised 2648 participants from 87 countries, contributing 105,196 paired nights. Each predictor was decomposed into within- and between-participant components by person-mean centering and entered a single linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept for participant, adjusted for age, body mass index (BMI), and sex. Outcomes were nocturnal mean glucose, nocturnal glucose coefficient of variation (CV), and nocturnal time in range (70-110 mg/dL). Per-participant slopes were fitted in participants with sustained wear (at least 30 nights spanning at least 60 days). Estimates were re-derived under trimming and robust-regression specifications and refitted within BMI and regional strata. Results: Higher average sleeping HR was associated with higher nocturnal mean glucose both within participants (+5.7 mg/dL per 10 bpm, 95% CI 5.4-5.9) and between participants (+6.5 mg/dL, 95% CI 5.6-7.3; both P<.001). Within participants, higher sleeping HR was also associated with higher glucose CV (+1.37 percentage points, 95% CI 1.30-1.43) and lower time in range (-6.3 percentage points, 95% CI -6.7 to -6.0). Of the 911 sustained-wear participants, 701 (76.9%, 95% CI 74.1%-79.6%) had a positive individual slope (median of +5.2 mg/dL per 10 bpm). The association survived in every BMI stratum and in all 5 regional strata. Sleep-duration irregularity was associated with mean glucose between participants (+4.1 mg/dL per 30 minutes, 95% CI 2.6-5.7) but only weakly within them (+0.23 mg/dL). Within participants, a night 1 standard deviation above a participants own mean sleeping HR corresponded to 2.5 mg/dL higher nocturnal mean glucose. Conclusions: Average sleeping HR was associated with glucose within individuals as well as between them, indicating that the relationship is not attributable solely to stable between-person differences and reflects, at least in part, night-to-night covariation. The association was modest, but discernible in naturalistic sleep across geographies. Sleep-duration irregularity was associated with nocturnal glycemia mainly between individuals.

items.title_en: From non-uptake during early adolescence to acceptance during a catch-up campaign: a qualitative study of changing HPV vaccination decisions across two life stages among young women in Amsterdam, the Netherlands
items.abstract_en: Background: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination effectively prevents HPV-related disease, but its population-level impact depends on sufficient coverage. In 2023-2024, the Netherlands offered free HPV vaccination to individuals aged 19-27 years through a national catch-up campaign. For women, this was a second opportunity, as they had been offered vaccination at ages 9-13 through the National Immunisation Programme (NIP). Back then, uptake was relatively low (46-57% in these birth cohorts), but uptake increased to 55-63% following the catch-up vaccination. This campaign provided an apt opportunity to explore the factors underlying previous and current HPV vaccination decisions among the same women across two life stages. Methods: Between May 2023 and May 2024, 16 semi-structured interviews were conducted in Amsterdam with women who accepted HPV vaccination during the catch-up after non-uptake during early adolescence. Interviews explored factors influencing non-uptake and later acceptance, guided by the Health Belief Model and additional sociocultural constructs. Data were analysed using thematic analysis with open and theory-guided coding in MAXQDA. Results: Non-uptake during early adolescence was primarily shaped by parental decision-making, cultural and religious norms, fear of side effects, low perceived susceptibility to HPV and limited self-efficacy. Acceptance in young adulthood was driven by greater autonomy, higher perceived susceptibility, increased trust in accumulated vaccine evidence and accessible vaccination infrastructure. Peer influence replaced parental influence as the dominant social factor. Conclusion: HPV vaccine decision-making is a dynamic process rather than fixed. Permanent catch-up HPV vaccination opportunities would enable young adults to make autonomous vaccination decisions as their circumstances change.

items.title_en: Stage-dependent associations of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome with Cognitive Decline, Depression, and Neuroimaging Signatures in multi-regional older adults
items.abstract_en: Background Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a multisystem condition associated with adverse outcomes, yet its impact on age-related cognitive health remains understudied. We examined associations of CKM with neurocognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes, modifiable physical and psychosocial factors contributing to cognitive impairment across CKM stages, and neuroimaging correlates. Methods Global aging cohorts (mean follow-up 6.5 years) and the Cohort Studies of Memory in an International Consortium (5.4 years) were used. CKM stages (0-4) were defined according to AHA framework. Longitudinal domain-specific cognitive changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models, and depressive symptoms using generalized linear regression with individual participant data approach. Population-attributable fractions were estimated for six modifiable factors associated with cognitive impairment across CKM stages. Cross-sectional associations with 34 neuroimaging biomarkers were examined in UK Biobank. Results Among 28,242 participants, advanced CKM stages (3-4) were associated with accelerated cognitive decline, particularly in attention, executive function, and language. Associations were stronger in younger individuals, men, and those with less education, but not modified by APOE 4 status. Advanced CKM stages were associated with depressive symptoms among cognitively unimpaired individuals. Modifiable factors accounted for 24.8% of cognitive impairment risk across CKM stages, mainly social isolation (7.0%), depressive symptoms (5.2%), and physical inactivity (5.2%). Advanced CKM stages were linked to widespread MRI alterations (27 biomarkers), especially white matter hyperintensity. Conclusion Advanced CKM stages are associated with accelerated cognitive decline and greater cerebrovascular burden. Addressing psychosocial factors and physical inactivity, alongside management of CKM risk factors, may help reduce cognitive impairment.

items.title_en: COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE AND ATTITUDE TOWARDS POLIO IMMUNIZATION IN NORTHERN NIGERIA
items.abstract_en: ckground: Poliomyelitis remains a public health concern where population immunity is incomplete and circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus (cVDPV) persists. Although Nigeria interrupted wild poliovirus transmission in 2020, cVDPV cases continue to pose challenges, particularly in parts of Northern Nigeria. Methods: This multicentre descriptive cross-sectional study evaluated community knowledge and attitudes towards polio immunization across 37 Local Government Areas (LGAs) in 20 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). A multistage sampling strategy was utilized to select 1,850 adult respondents (50 per LGA) spanning rural, semi-urban, and urban settlements. Results: Overall, 40.4% (n = 747) of respondents demonstrated good knowledge, while 58.4% (n = 1,080) displayed positive attitudes towards polio immunization. A striking disparity was observed across residence classifications: respondents in urban/semi-urban LGAs exhibited significantly higher levels of good knowledge (51.7%, 569/1,100) compared to those in rural LGAs (23.7%, 178/750; {chi} 2 = 144.00, df = 1, p < 0.001). Main sources of information were health workers (33.0%) and radio (21.1%). Conclusion: Knowledge deficits persist in rural Northern Nigerian communities despite favorable attitudes. Interventions must prioritize localized risk communication, traditional and religious leadership involvement, and primary healthcare integration.

items.title_en: pyTransRate: 1 reference-free quality assessment of de novo transcriptome assemblies with current aligners and quantifiers
items.title_zh: pyTransRate：利用现有比对器和定量工具对从头转录组组装进行无参考质量评估
items.abstract_en: Summary: The original software TransRate scores a de novo transcriptome assembly by mapping the reads it was built from back to it, with no reference required. Its last release (1.0.3) depends on Ruby 2.2 and on aligner and quantifier versions that can no longer be installed on most systems. pyTransRate is a Python reimplementation of the TransRate method built on snap-aligner 2.0.5 and salmon 2.7.0. In 5,031 paired comparisons (39 assembly-level metrics on each of 129 public assemblies), it reproduces the original sequence metrics and read counts exactly and ranks assemblies consistently with 1.0.3 (Spearman rho = 0.94 for assembly score, 0.98 for good-mapping rate), although its read-based scores are not numerically interchangeable with the original. It also reads gzip- and bgzip-compressed input directly. Availability and Implementation: pyTransRate is implemented in Python 3 and is freely available under the MIT license at https://github.com/macmanes-lab/pytransrate. It runs on Linux and macOS; snap-aligner and salmon are installed from Bioconda. Supplementary information: Supplementary data are available online. Supplementary Table S1 lists the assembly and read accessions for every assembly analyzed; Supplementary Table S2 gives per-assembly values from both implementations.

items.title_en: On the stability of learning
items.abstract_en: Learning algorithms are usually analyzed under the assumption that informative gradients are continuously available. But this is not always true---learning signals in biological neural networks, for example, may be sparse, local, and only intermittently available at any given synapse. In this work, we show that if gradient information is noisy and only intermittently available, learning may be unstable. In particular, even if average learning dynamics converge to the correct optimum, variance in learning may be asymptotically infinite. We explore this point in a number of analytically tractable settings, including single-layer and multi-layer linear networks, and derive explicit conditions under which learning is stable. These conditions complement, but are conceptually distinct from, existing conditions related to the stability of stochastic gradient descent. Our work demonstrates that unbiased credit assignment is not enough for reliable learning; sufficiently frequent and informative feedback is also required, which yields an additional constraint on models of biologically plausible learning.

items.title_en: Dynamic heart rate variability for classification of arrhythmia burden
items.abstract_en: Purpose: Heart rate variability (HRV) may provide information beyond heart rate (HR) for identifying arrhythmia burden, but the value of temporal HRV variation remains unclear. This study developed a dynamic HRV measure quantifying the interquartile range of window-level root mean square of successive RR-interval differences (IQRRMSSD) and evaluated its utility in classifying total abnormal-beat and premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden compared with the conventional RR-based HRV measure, RMSSD. Methods: Manually annotated 30-minute ECG recordings from 43 individuals were analyzed using overlapping windows. A linear support vector classifier was used to classify individuals as having high or low arrhythmia burden, defined using 1% and 10% burden thresholds. Four feature sets were evaluated: HR alone, HR with RMSSD, HR with IQRRMSSD, and all three measures. Performance was assessed using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation. Results: HRV-containing feature sets generally outperformed HR alone, depending on outcome and threshold. At the 1% threshold, IQRRMSSD showed particularly high sensitivity for total abnormal-beat and PVC burden ($0.970 \pm 0.064$ and $0.882 \pm 0.193$, respectively). At the 10% threshold, conventional RMSSD showed the strongest overall discrimination, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.947 for PVC burden. Combined features sometimes improved the sensitivity-specificity balance but not overall discrimination. Conclusion: These findings suggest that a conventional RR-based HRV measure is informative for elevated ectopic burden, while a dynamic HRV measure may provide complementary information for lower-burden abnormalities.

items.title_en: A theory of noisy linear recurrent neural network learning dynamics
items.title_zh: 含噪线性循环神经网络学习动力学理论
items.abstract_en: Biological neural networks are noisy: their dynamics involve difficult-to-predict fluctuations which are likely due not just to chaos, but also to a variety of low-level biophysical processes. Despite the omnipresence of intrinsic noise, its theoretical consequences are incompletely understood, especially in the context of learning. For example, does noise meaningfully shape representation learning, or is it better viewed as a nuisance factor whose presence or absence changes little about what solution is found and when? Here, we argue that intrinsic noise can significantly modulate representation learning in recurrent neural networks (RNNs), since it can strongly break solution-space degeneracies and in some cases control whether a non-degenerate solution exists at all. We show that this is true for an analytically tractable model of noisy RNN learning with a linear activation function and white noise inputs. We find that, in the so-called rich regime (where weights are initialized with small values), noise strongly modulates the directions in which the read-in, readout, and recurrent weights align. Moreover, we find that noise produces a kind of phase transition: for sufficiently high noise, a non-degenerate solution is not even optimal if parameter scales are limited (e.g., via regularization). These results extend recent analytic work on RNN representation learning and show that noise can act as a fundamental determinant of representations.

items.title_en: Phase response approach to networked neural activity models with delays
items.abstract_en: Networks of delay-coupled neural mass models alternate between synchrony and anti-phase locking as the delay between brain regions increases. The origin of these delay-dependent bands has remained unclear. Here, we show that a single function, the phase interaction function $H$ of an isolated node, predicts where the bands occur and explains why they repeat. For a Wilson--Cowan model with intra-nodal delay $τ$ and inter-nodal delay $ρ$, we compute the limit cycle and phase response, and hence $H$, by harmonic balance. Each band boundary is a zero of $H'$ shifted by the phase lag $Ωρ$, so the bands repeat in $ρ$ with the oscillation period. Simulations of the full delay-differential networks confirm these predictions, from two nodes, where predicted frequencies agree to second order in the coupling strength, to rings, where the theory also identifies coexisting stable twisted states that random initial conditions rarely reach. At weak coupling, the delays at which synchrony gains or loses stability are set by the node dynamics alone, whereas stable anti-phase states require a bipartite network. For a macaque connectome, metastability peaks at the edges of the synchrony bands, where the stability margin of phase-locking vanishes. The reduction is accurate for coupling strengths well below the slowest Floquet exponent of the node, beyond which a phase--amplitude description is needed. More broadly, vanishing phase-locking stability provides a simple route to metastability in delay-coupled oscillator networks and a candidate mechanism for the flexible coordination of brain dynamics.

items.title_en: Multiscale MIGHT: Modeling Local and Systemic Particle Transport in the Cardiovascular System
items.abstract_en: Analytical models of signaling molecule (SM) transport in the cardiovascular system (CVS) force a choice between whole-body scope and vessel-level resolution: Pharmacokinetic models for systemic transport lump each organ and lack small-scale structure, whereas synthetic molecular communication (MC) channel models resolve branched vessel networks (VNs) only for a single pass or capture recirculation only in topologically simple loops, and only partially include SM degradation. To close this gap, we propose Multiscale MIGHT, an extension of the Mixture of Inverse Gaussians for Hemodynamic Transport (MIGHT) model that jointly captures branched topologies, closed-loop circulation, organ clearance, and chemical degradation of SMs. First, we connect the ends of a branched VN to form a closed loop with local and global SM degradation, model the closed-loop channel impulse response for arbitrary transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) positions as a Laplace-domain feedback system, and approximate it in closed form by an inverse Gaussian mixture over multi-pass trajectories. The model is validated against finite-element simulations in COMSOL. Second, we set up a whole-body model, where an exemplary local VN, resolved at vessel-level detail, is embedded into the remaining systemic circulation, represented by lumped organ blocks. We simulate whole-body SM transport for various Tx sites and SM species. Our results show that, at an Rx in a local VN, only the initial pass produces a distinct peak in the SM concentration, significantly shaped by the local vasculature in case of small Tx-Rx distances; subsequent passes arrive strongly dispersed and are shaped almost entirely by organ clearance and chemical degradation rather than by the local VN topology.

items.title_en: Escaping cells dilute CRISPR screen responses unequally across cell types
items.abstract_en: Single-cell CRISPR screens run in many cell types are used to compare how cell types respond to perturbation, to train models that transfer effects between them and to score such models. These uses assume that cells carrying a guide RNA had their target knocked down. Yet cells grow for days before sequencing: when an essential gene is knocked down, knocked-down cells are depleted or stop dividing while cells that escaped knockdown keep growing, and the measured response, an average over all cells carrying the guide, is diluted. We define the escape fraction of a perturbation as the share of its measured cells whose target was not effectively knocked down, and estimate it from each cell's counts of the targeted gene with a two-group mixture that recovers known fractions in simulated mixtures. In most cell types the escape fraction rises with how essential the gene is, it is higher in a later screen of the same cells, and it reaches about half of the measured cells in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). It predicts how much each response is diluted: the response size falls to (1 - e)^2 of that of the knocked-down cells. Because the escape fraction differs between cell types, it changes all three uses: hESCs respond like K562 cells unless knockdown depletes them, the coefficient a simple transfer model learns is lowered by the dilution of the cell type it predicts, and a benchmark scored on all cells rewards predictions shrunk towards no change, partly because that ground truth is itself diluted. Where cells stop dividing instead, the response also contains expression differences between cell-cycle stages. Response sizes should be compared on knocked-down cells or corrected for the escape fraction.

items.title_en: ESX-1 substrates ESAT-6 and CFP-10 limit cGAS-STING activation via DNA and Zn2+ restriction
items.title_zh: ESX-1底物ESAT-6和CFP-10通过限制DNA和Zn2+抑制cGAS-STING激活
items.abstract_en: ESX-1-mediated phagosomal permeabilization exposes mycobacterial DNA to cytosolic cGAS-STING surveillance, yet the response is not overwhelming, suggesting additional layers of control exist. Here we show that the ESX-1 substrates ESAT-6 and CFP-10 constrain cGAS activation through complementary biochemical mechanisms. Purified Mycobacterium tuberculosis CFP-10 is a metal-dependent, 5'-3' exonuclease-like enzyme that preferentially degrades linear DNA, limiting the availability of stimulatory ligand. By contrast, purified M. tuberculosis ESAT-6 binds Zn2+ and limits the Zn2+-dependent conditions required for cGAS activation. During M. marinum infection, loss of these substrates augmented interferon-associated responses. Wild-type alleles restored immune suppression, whereas DNA-processing-defective CFP-10 or Zn2+-binding-defective ESAT-6 variants did not. These genotype-dependent differences were largely abolished in cGas-/- and Sting-/- macrophages. The double mutant was attenuated in zebrafish and mice, and its enhanced immune activation and attenuation were markedly diminished in cGas-/- mice. Prior exposure to the mutant improved zebrafish survival following wild-type challenge. Thus, beyond enabling mycobacterial DNA access to the cytosol, ESX-1 deploys its substrates to constrain cGAS-STING signaling by controlling activating-ligand availability and the metal-dependent environment required for sensor activation.

items.title_en: Simplifying complexity: the reliability of lidar-derived forest structural complexity metrics for conservation management
items.title_zh: 简化复杂性：激光雷达衍生森林结构复杂性指标在保护管理中的可靠性
items.abstract_en: Abstract 1. Forest structural complexity is regarded as a driver of biodiversity. The restructuring of forests to increase structural complexity is now a common objective of forest restoration and conservation projects. Lidar provides an efficient means of monitoring forest structure; however, the reliability of lidar-derived structural complexity metrics remains uncertain. Most metrics require a choice of resolution (such as pixel or voxel size), and whilst metric outcomes are sensitive to this choice, an understanding of how this impacts subsequent ecological interpretations of forest restoration monitoring is missing. 2. We assess how metric resolution choices impact FSC estimates using terrestrial laser scanning data from 32 single-species forest plots in Cairngorms National Park, Scotland. These plots represent four contrasting structural categories: ancient woodland (AW), old plantation (OP), old plantation with restructuring management (OPM) and natural restoration (NR); with a hypothesised order of complexity: AW, OPM, OP, NR (from highest complexity to lowest). We computed 21 FSC metrics and calculated how each metric ranked our forest structural categories across a resolution gradient (0.02-1.5m). We evaluated the stability of metric rankings across resolution values, their ability to discriminate forest categories, and the consistency of ecological interpretation of forest management targets. 3. Nine metrics produced unstable rankings, indicating that ecological conclusions were sensitive to resolution selection. Stable metrics discriminated well between categories with obvious structural differences but failed to discriminate between categories with subtle differences, particularly OP and OPM. 4. AW did not consistently exhibit the highest structural complexity, instead occupying an intermediate position characterised by a combination of canopy occupancy, openness and height inequality, not captured by any single metric. 5. We conclude that methodological choices can influence FSC estimates and ecological conclusions drawn from them. 6. Synthesis and applications: Reliable assessment of forest restoration depends not only on the choice of metric but also on how that metric is parameterised. We recommend transparent reporting and justification of resolution parameter selection together with the use of stable metrics that capture structural characteristics relevant to management objectives being monitored, to improve reliability and comparability of lidar-based forest monitoring.

items.title_en: Genomic detection of domoic acid biosynthesis uncovers expanded toxigenic diversity across Pseudo-nitzschia diatoms
items.title_zh: 软骨藻酸生物合成的基因组检测揭示伪菱形藻属硅藻中毒性多样性扩大
items.abstract_en: Domoic acid (DA) production by diatom genus Pseudo-nitzschia causes recurrent harmful algal blooms with major consequences for marine ecosystems, fisheries, and human health. Predicting DA risk remains challenging because toxin production varies across morphologically similar and cryptic lineages. Consequently, morphology or single marker genes often fail to resolve toxigenic potential. Here, we expand genomic resources for Pseudo-nitzschia by generating and compiling high-quality genomes spanning diverse species and biogeographic origins, establishing a genus-wide phylogenomic framework to investigate the distribution and evolution of the DA biosynthesis (dab) gene cluster. Among chemically characterized strains, the dab pathway was detected in species only with confirmed DA production. While the cluster exhibits a conserved core structure, several lineages display signatures of ongoing evolution, including intronization, locus rearrangement, and pseudogenization. One striking example of dab variation occurs in toxigenic P. australis strains, in which its biochemically validated isodomoic acid A synthase-encoding gene dabC is located outside the dab locus. Metatranscriptomic surveys reveal widespread environmental dab expression across size classes and species, implicating taxa not typically associated with environmental DA events, such as P. cf. obtusa and P. cf. plurisecta. To connect dab expression with chemical output, nutrient limitation experiments in the historically inconsistent DA producer P. pseudodelicatissima combined transcriptional profiling and nontargeted metabolomics demonstrating coordinated dab expression across distinct co-expression modules and DA accumulation in response to silicon limitation. Together, these results refine the phylogenetic scope of DA production and provide a genome-resolved basis for improved molecular monitoring of toxigenic diversity.

items.title_en: Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases
items.title_zh: 知识图谱尺度的Phenologs：面向数千种人类疾病的从小鼠到黏菌的候选基因目录
items.abstract_en: Model organisms carry decades of systematic gene-phenotype annotation, but connecting those annotations to human disease is rarely straightforward. Phenologs offer a principled way to bridge this gap. A human disease and a model-organism phenotype are phenologs when their associated genes, linked by orthology, overlap more than expected by chance, so the genes of one become candidates for the other. Here we compute phenologs from the Monarch Knowledge Graph, which integrates gene-disease, gene-phenotype and orthology data for human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families as orthogroups and a 5% false discovery rate estimated from 1,000 randomized networks, we identify 61,243 phenologs between 3,752 human diseases and 9,700 model-organism phenotypes. We introduce a hypergeometric scheme for ranking the candidate genes a disease's phenologs nominate and compare it with the naive Bayes scheme of the original phenolog studies. Both methods recover held-out genes within a disease at similar rates, but only the hypergeometric score can be compared across diseases. Using a one-year-older release of the graph, the top 100 candidates per disease recovered 9 of 73 gene-disease associations added since, 23.5 times the random-gene expectation. Mouse accounts for most of these, with zebrafish, worm and fission yeast each contributing associations that mouse does not. We release per-disease gene candidate rankings, with known and novel associations flagged, and a dashboard for exploration of our results.

items.title_en: Building virtual cell dynamics that evolve with biological measurements
items.title_zh: 构建随生物学测量演化的虚拟细胞动力学
items.abstract_en: Virtual cell models built from single-cell measurements need to predict how cells change over time, but new biological measurements often reveal dynamical relationships that existing models cannot express. Translating such measurements into dynamics therefore requires deciding what biological relation should be modeled, where it should enter the formulation and how its recovery should be validated. Here we present CellCompass, an agentic AI system that couples a scientific agent with an extensible dynamical engine for modeling state transitions and population change, along with fate and molecular readout. CellCompass reuses existing formulations when sufficient and designs, implements and refines new ones when experimental measurements introduce additional constraints. To assess this capability, we developed DynBench100, a benchmark of 100 simulated single-cell time-course scenarios with hidden dynamical ground truth. CellCompass achieved the highest aggregate performance among the tested general-purpose and biomedical agents across six dynamical tasks. Across four real single-cell studies, it retained an existing velocity-growth model to reconstruct context-dependent epithelial-mesenchymal transition and developed three new dynamical formulations for distinct experimental measurements. In drug-response data, incorporating metabolic RNA labeling reduced pulse-control identifiability error by 31.1%, revealing staged response programs and generating testable predictions for perturbing a candidate adaptive program. In hematopoietic lineage tracing, incorporating clonal barcodes improved clone-fate agreement by 54% over the strongest dynamical baseline, identifying early lineage priming among transcriptionally similar progenitors. Finally, in time-resolved CITE-seq data, CellCompass reduced future surface-protein distribution error by 13.2% for RNA-initialized trajectories, uncovering lineage-specific temporal offsets between transcriptional and protein programs. Together, CellCompass provides a framework in which virtual-cell dynamics can expand with the biological measurements used to constrain them.

items.title_en: A maximum entropy model for m6A prediction: from human transcripts to influenza A viral segments
items.title_zh: 用于m6A预测的最大熵模型：从人类转录本到甲型流感病毒片段
items.abstract_en: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most frequent mRNA modification in eukaryotic cells and is involved in the regulation of gene expression. Since viruses can hijack the host machinery to perform this chemical editing, m6A is also involved in viral replication and innate immune system activation. Nowadays only few m6A viral maps are available, making complementary methods crucial to accelerate the investigation of these mechanisms. Here we propose MEMAR, a Maximum Entropy model, to predict the methylation frequency, depending on the eight-mers nucleotide motif surrounding the central adenosine. MEMAR is a fast, simple and modular model: it can be trained on human methylation maps and refined including the methylation level per transcript and the position of motifs relatively to the coding regions. This modularity allows strong adaptability, leading MEMAR to better perform over influenza A segments than the mammalian state-of-the-art DeepSRAMP method. MEMAR generalization potential is assessed on i) human transcripts from GLORI and miCLIP experiments ii) HEK293T and HeLa cell lines iii) positive and negative influenza A viral segments and iv) altered-methylation experiments. A two-state dynamical model between m6A writers and erasers explains MEMAR predictive power as a function of the global methylation percentage, and allows us to interpret anomalies in altered conditions through variations of methylation or de-methylation binding constants.

items.title_en: Stochasticity in Metabolism: Oxidative Stress Response Phenotypes As Emergent Consequences of Network Topology
items.title_zh: 代谢中的随机性：氧化应激响应表型作为网络拓扑的涌现结果
items.abstract_en: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are ubiquitous yet elusive due to their reactivity and short half-lives, making simulation essential for mechanistic insight. Traditional ROS modeling has been confined to small ODE frameworks limited by kinetic-parameter scarcity. Here, we recast ROS dynamics as a flux-balance analysis (FBA) optimization problem using COBRA and CPLEX, augmenting the Escherichia coli iJO1366 genome-scale model with 84 spontaneous oxidation, 14 redox, and 9 detoxification reactions, targeting three ROS species: hydroxyl radicals, superoxide, and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). We also formalize five fundamental rules of oxidation biology in the form of mixed-integer linear constraints, allowing us to dynamically incorporate reaction rate constants and let complex behavior emerge from first principles. Among these phenomena is the bimodal killing pattern under H2O2 stress, first announced over 40 years ago and never computationally recapitulated until now. We observe it by stochastically sampling our models with GapSplit, simulating bet-hedging and partitioning solutions into growers, persisters, and non-survivors. In our simulations, this killing effect arises solely from the metabolic network topology during random exploration of alternative metabolic configurations. The conservation of steady state creates a stochastic bias for detoxification when central carbon metabolism reaches its metabolic capacity to deal with ROS, causing the famous survival recovery phase. The recovery phase is thus part of Mode 1 metabolism, characterized by spare detoxification capacity and fulfilled by the Ahp reaction in E. coli. Mode 2 has no spare detoxification. We anticipate this to be an overlooked universal principle.

items.title_en: Ancestral tributyltin exposure produces male-specific brown adipose thermogenic dysregulatoin
items.title_zh: 祖代三丁基锡暴露导致雄性特异性棕色脂肪产热失调
items.abstract_en: Obesity is a global health challenge increasingly linked to environmental obesogens. Tributyltin (TBT), a model obesogen that activates PPARgamma and RXR, promotes transgenerational obesity in mice, but whether developmental and ancestral exposure impairs energy balance remains unclear. Brown adipose tissue (BAT) contributes to energy expenditure and thermoregulation through UCP1-dependent and -independent pathways. We tested whether TBT exposure disrupts BAT function in F1 and F3 descendants of exposed F0 dams. We measured body composition before and after high-fat diet (HFD) challenge and assessed resting core body temperature, BAT gene expression, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) content, and mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) capacity. TBT-line males accumulated more fat after HFD without changes in lean mass despite similar mass-scaled food intake. Before HFD, core body temperature was lower in F1 and F3 TBT-line males, indicating impaired thermal homeostasis before increased adiposity. Candidate-gene qPCR did not show uniform suppression of thermogenic genes; instead, Ucp1 mRNA increased while Ucp2 mRNA decreased in F1 males, indicating dysregulation. Transcriptomal profiling revealed altered thermogenic signaling and consistent downregulation of mitochondrial electron transport chain genes across F1 and F3 males. Relative mtDNA content was unchanged, whereas complex-specific respirometry revealed reduced complex I- and II-associated respiratory capacity, providing evidence of impaired electron transport. No consistent effects occurred in females. These findings identified an early, male-associated BAT phenotype characterized by thermogenic dysregulation, reduced mitochondrial ETC capacity, and impaired thermal homeostasis. They support a model in which impaired BAT mitochondrial function contributes to later susceptibility to diet-induced obesity.

items.title_en: Natural scene segmentation dynamics reveal iterative Bayesian inference
items.title_zh: 自然场景分割动力学揭示迭代贝叶斯推断
items.abstract_en: The visual system operates by segmenting visual inputs into distinct perceptual objects. Segmentation is dynamic, as revealed by the tempo of perceptual choices and neural activity in the visual cortex. Dynamics for natural stimuli however, are poorly understood because natural scene segmentation is ambiguous and subjective. We measured subjective human segmentation maps for natural images using an innovative paradigm, and uncovered richer spatiotemporal dynamics than predicted by current theories of segmentation. To explain these dynamics, we introduced Iterative Bayesian Inference algorithms for segmentation that iteratively integrate visual inputs with the prior expectation for local smoothness. When visual inputs were consistent with such a spatial prior, iterative inference was faster. Such a predicted relationship between spatial prior and inferential dynamics was evident in our data and correctly reflected each individual participant's spatial biases. We conclude that iterative Bayesian inference sets the tempo for a fundamental function of natural vision.

items.title_en: Timed binary WNT activity is sufficient to model the early human neural axis
items.abstract_en: The vertebrate nervous system develops into functionally distinct domains along the body axis[1]. Developmental studies implicate multiple signaling pathways in coordinating this process, but the order of specification events, sufficiency of individual signals, and molecular basis of competency remain unclear [2,3], leaving the field without a unified model of neuraxis patterning. Enteric nervous system (ENS) and midbrain dopaminergic (mDA) progenitors have reached clinical and preclinical testing [4-11], yet neither is produced at full purity, and yields vary markedly across human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) lines, reflecting incomplete control of axial identity. Here we use single-cell genetic fate mapping to demonstrate that hPSCs can commit to anterior or posterior cranial fate within the first 24 hours of differentiation, before neural induction. Building on this finding, we show that the duration of a single saturating WNT pulse is sufficient to specify three 'first-order' domains: anterior cranial (0 h), posterior cranial (24 h) and trunk (48 h), each pre-neural and competent for CNS, neural crest and epidermal lineages. Nested 'second-order' domains are specified within first-order domains in response to WNT, FGF, and retinoic acid. Mechanistically, an anterior gene regulatory network repressing WNT targets is irreversibly shut down during the transition to posterior identities. Applying this binary WNT patterning logic, we generate mDA neurons and ENS progenitors robustly across hPSC lines and establish an assembloid model combining first-order progenitors to produce all major regions of the nervous system.

items.title_en: Delayed bleaching-induced coral mortality limits reef recovery after a marine heatwave
items.abstract_en: Coral reefs worldwide are increasingly exposed to marine heatwaves, which cause recurrent coral bleaching and mass mortality events. While the immediate impact of bleaching has been extensively studied, the longer-term consequences and recovery trajectories remain poorly understood. By integrating two long-term monitoring datasets, we quantified how fine-scale variation in heat stress exposure shaped post-bleaching trajectories. We examined patterns of coral mortality and recovery across 13 sites in Mo'orea (French Polynesia) after the most severe marine heatwave recorded on the island in 2019. The maximum accumulated heat stress (AHSmax) varied between sites (from 5.76 to 6.26 {degrees}C weeks), allowing the assessment of heat stress-related mortality between coral genera. Pocillopora mortality increased with AHSmax, and mean coral cover collapsed from 35% to 17% within one year. Acropora experienced consistently high mortality rates across all sites (median: 84%), reducing mean cover from 5% to 1%. Six years of tracking individual Pocillopora colonies revealed strong size-dependent bleaching responses. The heatwave increased the probability of complete and partial mortality more in large than in small Pocillopora colonies. Remarkably, elevated partial mortality persisted for at least three years after the thermal stress had subsided, indicating substantial delayed impacts. Contrary to the rapid recovery historically observed on Mo'orea's reefs following other disturbances, coral cover continued to decline for four years after the bleaching event, with no evidence of recovery. Our findings reveal that bleaching impacts extend far beyond the heatwave itself. Persistent delayed mortality of surviving colonies can limit reef recovery for years, indicating that post-bleaching demographic processes may be a major, yet underappreciated, determinant of coral reefs' resilience.

items.title_en: A peptidomimetic inhibitor blocks Vibrio cholerae adhesin FrhA.
items.abstract_en: Cholera is a diarrheal disease resulting from colonization of the small intestine by the Gram-negative bacterium Vibrio cholerae. The peptide-binding domain (PBD) of the adhesion protein FrhA is critical for V. cholerae intestinal colonization and biofilm formation. Antagonists of the FrhA-PBD were designed based on the tripeptide motif H-Trp-Thr-Asp-OH. Constraining the N-terminal tryptophan as a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-{beta}-carboline-3-carboxylic acid (Tcc) residue and X-ray analysis of a co-crystal with the FrhA-PBD define the minimal inhibitory motif. Moreover, H-(R)-Tcc-Thr-Asp-OH exhibited nanomolar binding affinity (Kd = 101 {+/-} 30.2 nM) to the FrhA-PBD, blocking adhesion protein-mediated bacterial hemagglutination and reducing biofilm formation in vitro. Intestinal epithelial cell adhesion to the FrhA-PBD was also blocked by the Tcc tripeptide (IC50 = 24 M; 95% CI, 11-51 M), which resisted chymotrypsin proteolysis.
