The activity of this peptidomimetic inhibitor and the atomic-level understanding of FrhA-PBD binding provide insights for developing anti-adhesion therapies to treat cholera.

items.title_en: DNA-directed nanometer-scale integration of single colloidal quantum emitters with on-chip photonics
items.title_zh: DNA引导的单胶体量子发射器与片上光子学的纳米尺度集成
items.abstract_en: Incorporating colloidal quantum emitters into integrated photonics would greatly advance quantum optics. However, placing individual sub-10 nm colloidal particles onto micron-sized photonic structures with nanometer-scale precision remains challenging. We introduce topography-modulated origami placement, which uses DNA origami to place colloidal nanomaterials within lithographically defined, shape-matched resist wells. The method patterns origami templates onto photonic chips with high yield and nanometer-scale precision. A soft-silicification-passivation step stabilizes deposited origamis while preserving DNA binding sites that selectively attach and align colloidal quantum rods, controlling their position and emission polarization. Placed quantum rods demonstrated room-temperature single-photon emission. We integrated individual quantum rods with waveguides, micro-ring resonators, and bullseye microcavities, and achieved cavity-coupled single-photon emission. This approach offers a general platform for integrating colloidal quantum materials into photonic systems.

items.title_en: Species phylogenetics using intraprotein residue dependence inferred with protein foundation models
items.title_zh: 利用蛋白质基础模型推断的蛋白质内残基依赖性进行物种系统发育分析
items.abstract_en: Traditional molecular phylogenetic inference uses multiple sequence alignments and amino acid substitution models that generally assume that sites evolve independently. In contrast, protein foundation models (pFMs) are deep learning models that reveal residue dependence patterns within sequences. There are two types of pFMs: Evolutionary Scale Models (esm-pFM) for analyzing individual protein sequences, and MSA Transformer (msat-pFM) models for analyzing MSAs. Using pFMs to analyze sequences produces residue attention matrices (RAMs) and sequence attention matrices (SAMs), respectively. RAMs and SAMs can be used to estimate pairwise distances and, thus, reconstruct phylogenies using the Neighbor-Joining (NJ) method. Here, we compare the performance of RAM-NJ and SAM-NJ phylogenies in reconstructing established species relationships across different proteins and taxon sets. Surprisingly, RAM-NJ phylogenies were generally as accurate as SAM-NJ phylogenies even though RAM inference does not require construction or analysis of an MSA. Our results show that pFM-based analyses can recover species relationships without conventional substitution models or, in the case of RAMs, a multiple sequence alignment. These results suggest that evolutionary relationships are reflected not only in primary sequence differences between species, but also in the sequence-specific patterns of inter-residue dependence produced by pFM analysis of individual sequences. However, pFM phylogenies are less accurate than those obtained with standard maximum likelihood approaches, underscoring the need to further develop methods to harness RAMs and SAMs more effectively.

items.title_en: Targeting PRMT5 Across Cancers and AI-Driven Discovery of Candidate Compounds
items.title_zh: 靶向跨癌种PRMT5及AI驱动的候选化合物发现
items.abstract_en: Protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) is a promising anticancer target, yet existing inhibitors shown limited clinical efficacy. Here, we paired multi-omics pan-cancer profiling with a machine learning virtual screening pipeline. Bioinformatics analyses with TIMER3, GEPIA2, UALCAN/CPTAC, the Human Protein Atlas, cBioPortal, STRING and Enrichr revealed widespread of PRMT5 mRNA expression, protein abundance, survival, genetic alteration, immune infiltration and co-expression networks with tumor-specific prognostic impact in GBM, LGG and KIRC. A deep neural network screened about 1.5 million PubChem compounds and deep neural network reached a ROC-AUC = 0.9857 and prioritized three candidates, CID 44345182, CID 2794188 and CID 44345334. Subsequent molecular docking against PRMT5 (PDB ID: 4X61), ADMET filtering and toxicity prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations identified CID 44345182 as the potential hit, similar the docking scores of -9.8 compared with -9.2 kcal/mol for the reference ligand in binding affinity and trajectory stability. These findings clarify the context-dependent roles of PRMT5 and further experiment validations are needed to establish CID 44345182 as a promising candidate.

items.title_en: Collective directional memory controls the range of epithelial cell migration
items.abstract_en: Cell migration is a fundamental behavior involved in multicellular development, regeneration, and homeostasis, which is deregulated in cancer. Epithelial cells migrate individually when isolated and collectively within a tissue. However, how interactions between cells affect their ability to explore space and their sensitivity to guidance signals is poorly understood. Here, we show that isolated cells that are persistent random walkers adopt a superdiffusive behavior in an epithelium. The effect is stronger than external guidance cues and enables cells to reach greater distances than when isolated. This directional memory emerges from fractional Brownian motion that relies on velocity coordination between neighboring cells with intact cytoskeletal connections to intercellular adhesion complexes. Furthermore, we show how the stability and mechanosensitivity of adhesion complexes ultimately regulate the speed of collective migration and the sensitivity to guidance signals via dimerization of the adhesion protein vinculin. Together, our results show how cell speed, persistence, and directionality define the efficiency of spatial cell exploration on short, intermediate, and long time scales, respectively.

items.title_en: Single-Cell Atlas of Non-Functioning Gonadotroph Tumors and Anterior Pituitary Reveals Lineage Infidelity and Clinically Associated Transcriptional Programs
items.abstract_en: Non-functioning gonadotroph (NFG) tumors are the most common type of non-functioning pituitary adenomas and cause significant morbidity through mass effect. The molecular programs that distinguish NFG tumor cells from normal gonadotrophs and underlie tumor growth remain poorly understood. The aim of this study was to define transcriptional differences between NFG tumors and the normal anterior pituitary gland (APG) at single-cell resolution and to identify programs associated with tumor growth. We performed single-cell/nucleus RNA-sequencing of 21 NFG tumors and 8 APG samples, followed by integrative analyses of differential gene expression, regulatory networks, and cell-cell communication. We profiled 77,342 APG cells and 152,649 NFG tumor cells. Within the APG, we identified novel marker genes for each neuroendocrine cell type and distinct transcriptional signatures of anterior and posterior pituitary stem cell populations. Compared with normal gonadotrophs, tumor cells shared a core transcriptomic signature conserved across samples despite inter-tumor heterogeneity. Many conserved genes were markers of non-gonadotroph neuroendocrine and stem cells, suggesting that lineage infidelity is a recurrent feature of NFGs. Pseudobulk profiling identified genes positively correlated with tumor volume, including the known oncogenes CAD, BRF2, and SOX12. Finally, tumors showed increased proportions of myeloid, endothelial, and mural cells and crosstalk between tumor, immune, and stromal populations. This study defines transcriptomic signatures of cell identity in the normal APG and NFG tumors. Our findings reveal programs associated with NFG lineage infidelity and tumor growth, highlighting candidate predictors of patient outcomes and potential therapeutic targets.

items.title_en: The Cardiovascular Benefit of Menopause Hormone Treatment is Age-Dependent in Ldlr-/- Mice
items.abstract_en: Background: The risk of Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) increases in women after menopause, coinciding with declining estrogen levels. However, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) has not consistently reduced ASCVD events in post-menopausal women, despite improvements in lipid profiles. The mechanisms underlying the diminished cardiovascular protective effects of estrogens during MHT remain poorly understood. Methods: Atherosclerosis was established in 11-month-old female Ldlr-/- mice through Western diet feeding. To investigate the effects of menopause and 17{beta}-estradiol (E2) treatment on atherosclerotic burden during lipid normalization, mice were switched to a chow diet and subjected to ovariectomy (OVX) with and without E2 treatment. To determine the contribution of inflammation to ASCVD risk during MHT, a cohort of mice received Ifn{gamma}-/- bone marrow transplant (Ifn{gamma}-/-BM) before hormone treatment. To assess the influence of age on ASCVD risk during MHT, parallel studies were conducted in young mice, beginning at 12 weeks of age. Outcomes included lipid profiles, HDL function, circulating cytokines, atherosclerotic burden, liver lipid metabolic pathways and transcriptomic profiles, and hepatic estrogen receptor signaling. Results: OVX increased atherosclerotic burden compared with sham-operation. E2 treatment following OVX failed to reduce established atherosclerosis in older mice but reduced atherosclerosis in young mice during diet-induced lipid normalization. In older mice, E2 treatment increased circulating IFN&#947, impaired HDL antioxidant and cholesterol efflux functions, and promoted inflammatory and vulnerable plaque phenotypes. Suppression of inflammation through Ifn{gamma}-/-BM transplantation restored HDL function and the ability of E2 treatment to reduce atherosclerosis in older mice. In contrast, E2 treatment following OVX in young mice limited inflammation and improved HDL function. E2 treatment increased liver fatty acid metabolic signaling in both older and young mice but increased liver 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) levels only in older mice. This age-dependent response was associated with remodeling of hepatic estrogen receptor (ER) expression, characterized by reduced ER&#945 and increased in G protein-coupled ER expression with aging. Liver transcriptomic analyses identified inflammatory and interferon-associated signatures following OVX+E2 treatment in older mice. qPCR analyses across older and young mice suggested age-associated differences in inflammatory transcripts in response to E2. Conclusions: These findings suggest that aging alters the hepatic response to E2 treatment following ovariectomy, promoting oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling that contribute to persistent systemic inflammation and compromise the ability of E2 to reduce atherosclerosis.

items.title_en: Single-cell spatiotemporal transcriptomics reveals the origin, cellular heterogeneity and regulatory network of seed fiber cells in poplar
items.abstract_en: Poplar (Populus spp.) is globally important for timber and afforestation, and is also a model system for woody perennials. However, the molecular control of reproductive organ development, particularly that of the epidermal trichomes on seeds known as seed fibers (fluff), which cause environmental and health concerns, remains poorly understood. Here, integrating single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics, we constructed a spatiotemporal atlas of female poplar capsules that resolves the cellular composition of the organ and positions each cell type within its native tissue context. We traced the developmental trajectory of seed fibers, showing that they originate from placenta epidermal cells, and identified three functionally distinct fiber cell subtypes involved in initiation, photosynthesis and elongation. Network analysis identified candidate regulators including PtoPDF2, PtoMYB38 and PtoHDG11. PtoPDF2 activates PtoMYB38 and PtoSTK2 by binding L1-box motifs in their promoters, revealing a module that governs seed fiber initiation. Together, our study provides a framework for seed fiber development in poplar and candidate targets for breeding low-fluff cultivars.

items.title_en: GLP-1-receptor agonist use is associated with shorter survival in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and diabetes mellitus: a multicenter retrospective study
items.abstract_en: Background: Glucagon-like peptide-1receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are increasingly used to treat diabetes mellitus (DM) and obesity. However, their impact on the progression of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) among those with comorbid DM is unknown. Objective: We examined the relationship between GLP-1RA treatment and disease progression among people with ALS and DM. Methods: This multicenter retrospective chart review study used an electronic health record search at 14 institutions to identify consecutive patients with a confirmed ALS diagnosis and documented comorbid type 1 or type 2 DM. All charts were reviewed for demographics, disease history, medication use, and tracheostomy/survival status. Patients who did not meet Awaji ALS diagnostic criteria, lacked a documented history of DM, or had insufficient records were excluded. Tracheostomy-free survival was compared between the GLP-1RA group (exposed) and No-GLP-1RA group (unexposed) using Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age and region of onset (bulbar, respiratory, and diffuse, versus spinal). Results: A total of 308 ALS patients with comorbid DM were included from 14 institutions, of whom 39 (13%) were treated with one or more GLP-1RA. In the GLP-1RA group, diagnostic delay was shorter (10.2 vs 15.9 months, p<0.001), and revised ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) score decline from symptom onset to first measure was faster (1.5 vs 1.1 points/month, p=0.023) compared with the No-GLP-1RA group. Other baseline characteristics, including age, sex, race, region of onset, and first ALSFRS-R score, were not significantly different between groups. Tracheostomy-free survival from symptom onset was numerically shorter in the GLP-1RA group (median survival 27.0 vs 36.7 months; log-rank p=0.073). After adjusting for age and region of onset, GLP-1RA exposure was associated with an increased risk of tracheostomy or death (hazard ratio 1.56, 95% confidence interval 1.06-2.28, p=0.024). Conclusions: In this multicenter cohort, GLP-1RA treatment was associated with faster disease progression and shorter tracheostomy-free survival in people with ALS and comorbid DM.

items.title_en: DRIPS: Domain Randomisation for Image-based Perivascular spaces Segmentation
items.abstract_en: Background MRI-visible perivascular spaces (PVS) are an imaging marker of compromised brain health function. However, robust PVS segmentation remains challenging: conventional methods often require cohort-specific parameter tuning, while supervised deep-learning models depend on extensive manual annotations for training and may fail to generalise to unseen scanners, protocols, and clinical populations. Methods We introduce DRIPS (Domain Randomisation for Image-based PVS Segmentation), a fully automated deep-learning framework trained exclusively on synthetic data. By learning PVS representations from a plethora of simulated cases, DRIPS transfers to real-world MRI without using manually labelled PVS data from real participants. We evaluated DRIPS in 185 fully manually annotated MRI scans from eight independent cohorts encompassing diverse clinical populations and acquisition settings, including 3T and 7T imaging, T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences, and isotropic and anisotropic resolutions. DRIPS was compared with five previously published methods. Results Across cohorts, DRIPS significantly outperformed the second-best method for both area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) and centreline Dice similarity coefficient (clDice), with mean gains of at least 0.1: 0.146 for basal ganglia (BG) AUPRC (P = 0.008), 0.125 for centrum semiovale (CSO) AUPRC (P = 0.008), 0.112 for BG clDice (P = 0.016), and 0.186 for CSO clDice (P = 0.008). Importantly, its performance was not associated with white matter hyperintensity burden. Conclusions DRIPS enables accurate, fully automated PVS segmentation across heterogeneous imaging settings without the need for real PVS annotations for training.

items.title_en: BurnCare: A deep learning framework for burn injury assessment and TBSA estimation.
items.title_zh: BurnCare：用于烧伤评估和TBSA估计的深度学习框架
items.abstract_en: Background: Burn injuries disproportionately affect resource-limited settings. India alone reports over seven million burn injuries annually against only 67 dedicated burn centres. Consequently, initial assessments, such as total burn surface area (%TBSA), which directly influence fluid resuscitation and referral decisions, are frequently performed by non-specialist staff, with known inter-observer variability. Existing computer-assisted tools either require manual annotation on a generic 3D body model or estimate %TBSA using an anatomical approximation (the Rule of Nines) rather than from the patient's own segmented body area. Methods: We developed BurnCare, a deployable artificial intelligence-assisted web and Android-based platform that estimates %TBSA from a single smartphone photograph. The pipeline was developed as a two-stage deep learning system that first isolated the patient from the background (ResNet50 encoder, U-Net decoder) and then segmented the burn skin within that region (DenseNet169 encoder, U-Net decoder), with both stages trained on a prospectively collected, multi-device dataset from a tertiary burn centre in India. The platform supports %TBSA estimation both with scale calibration (using a surgical tape of known length) and without it. %TBSA estimated using BurnCare was compared with independent, blinded estimates from three healthcare professionals for 16 patient photographs, using Pearson's correlation coefficient, mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE) and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: The background-removal and burn-segmentation models achieved strong performance (intersection over union 0.9811 and 0.8504, respectively). BurnCare's automatic %TBSA estimate correlated strongly with the mean of three clinicians' estimates (r = 0.746, p < 0.001, MAE = 6.29, RMSE = 8.63 percentage points; n = 16), improving to r = 0.853 (MAE = 4.32, RMSE = 6.37) after manual mask correction; the ICC among the three clinicians alone was 0.728. Conclusions: A two-stage artificial intelligence-assisted platform, BurnCare, was developed. The platform supports burn detection and %TBSA using deep learning models trained on real-world patient datasets. The foreground prediction is supported by a hybrid ResNet50-U-Net, while burn skin prediction is supported by a DenseNet169-U-Net. BurnCare's %TBSA estimates agree with clinical judgement about as closely as clinicians agree with each other, supporting its use as a decision-support and documentation tool for burn triage in resource-limited settings. The dataset collected and the BurnCare platform are available online.

items.title_en: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
items.abstract_en: Learning molecular models of RNA requires simulation data that capture conformational variability and provide consistent physical training signals. Here, we introduce mdRNAcat, a curated dataset of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 48 RNA systems selected to promote sequence diversity. Each system is simulated using replica-exchange with solute scaling (REST2), with 32 Hamiltonian states and production lengths of 200-300 ns per state. The dataset provides atomic coordinates, instantaneous forces, and forces reevaluated under the unscaled reference Hamiltonian, together with structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata. Coordinates and forces are available at 1 ps intervals for the reference state and 100 ps intervals across all states in a standardized HDF5 format. We characterize conformational sampling, exchange behavior, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions to document the properties of the simulated ensembles. mdRNAcat provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating data-driven RNA models, including coarse-grained force fields.

items.title_en: Comparing Measurements of Pictorial Depth: Conditions for Placing Methods, Observers and Depiction Styles on One Scale
items.abstract_en: Two observers can agree about what lies in front in a picture yet report different amounts of apparent depth. People report pictorial depth by judging which of two points looks nearer, setting a probe to match a surface, adjusting relative sizes, or rating three-dimensionality. Two such methods can agree closely without sharing a unit. We ask when different methods, observers, depiction styles and viewing conditions can share one scale. Each set of scores, a measurement block, is a graph node. Two blocks are linked only if their shared observations pass six checks fixed in advance, among them outcome type, removal of declared offsets and position effects, proportionality and covariance. If the adjusted shared patterns are exactly proportional, a connected graph fixes every block's gain, its relative scale factor. The checks accept proportionality only within a set margin, so a link supports the gains without proving exact proportionality. One unit is still not one depth coordinate. Suppose each block scores shared stimuli with its own origin and positive unit. A matrix-rank test then decides when a common coordinate is identified: when only one overall origin and unit remain free. If each shared stimulus, an anchor, is scored by exactly two blocks, this needs two disjoint sets of anchors, each connecting every block, their compatibility assumed, not tested. They also suffice, except for anchor values satisfying exact polynomial relations (probability zero for anchor values drawn from any distribution with a density). We adapt network gain estimation from test linking, with a loop-consistency check. A reanalysis of published probe settings on 3-D renderings passes one of 171 candidate depiction-style links through all six checks, each judged by its own 95% bound, unadjusted for the 171 pairs. Links between tasks remain untested; they need shared stimuli and a joint uncertainty model.

items.title_en: Estimating the Direct Impact of Influenza Vaccination and Vaccine-Averted Illnesses Using an Extended Static Compartmental Model
items.abstract_en: A previously developed static compartment model informed influenza program decisions by estimating the direct impact of influenza vaccination. To improve the estimation of the burden averted by vaccination, we extended this model to consider multiple influenza seasons, allow natural and vaccine-induced immunity to wane over time allow influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) to differ by hospitalized versus non-hospitalized influenza-associated illness, and measure deaths averted. For model demonstration, we created a synthetic Northern Hemisphere-like and year-round influenza activity dataset spanning four seasons among older adults (>65 years) and assumed VE against symptomatic illness of 37% (17%-53%) and VE against hospitalization of 45% (28%-59%). Under Northern Hemisphere-like activity and an existing vaccination program with an average annual vaccine coverage of 33%, vaccination averted 15.1% (95% UI: 12.2%-16.3%) of influenza-associated illnesses across four seasons; the annual prevented fraction for hospitalized deaths ranged from 14.4% (95% UI: 11.7%-16.8%) to 18.5% (95% UI: 14.9%-21.5%). Under a hypothetical year-round vaccination program with an annual coverage of 20%, vaccination averted 4.9% (95% UI: 3.8%-5.4%) of influenza-associated illnesses across four seasons; the annual prevented fraction for hospitalized deaths ranged from 5.5% (95% UI: 4.3%-6.5%) and 5.8% (95% UI: 4.8%-6.6%). These model extensions allow estimation of vaccine-averted burden across multiple seasons and diverse vaccination program settings, providing information to support influenza vaccination decision-making.

items.title_en: Modelled mortality benefits of reducing fibrinolysis resistance in sepsis: integrating observational and ex vivo data
items.abstract_en: Background. Suppressed fibrinolysis (fibrinolysis resistance) is increasingly recognised as a driver of organ failure in sepsis, yet trials in sepsis-induced coagulopathy have largely targeted coagulation rather than fibrinolysis. This study combined an observational ICU cohort with nested analyses of plasma fibrinolysis proteins and ex vivo reversibility, modelling the potential mortality reduction from restoring fibrinolytic capacity to inform trial design. Methods. In 188 adults admitted to ICU with sepsis, repeated tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)-enhanced viscoelastometric testing quantified fibrinolysis resistance as the fibrin adjusted lysis time (TPA-LT/FIBA10) and as ordinal Grades 1-3 of worsening resistance. Adjusted logistic regression and time-varying Cox models related fibrinolysis resistance to death within 28 days of admission, with unmeasured confounding assessed by E-values. In nested sub-studies, plasma fibrinolysis proteins were measured and whole blood was tested ex vivo for reversal of resistance by supplemental tPA, plasminogen, or an inhibitory antibody to a2-antiplasmin (a2AP iAb). Ex vivo effects were modelled onto the observed fibrinolysis resistance-mortality relationship using a hypothetical intervention distribution framework. Results. Each e-fold (~2.72) increase in TPA-LT/FIBA10 was associated with a 2.2-fold (95% CI 1.5-3.3) increase in the odds of death in the fully adjusted logistic model and a 2.3-fold (1.6-3.2) increased hazard in the time-varying Cox model. Comparing the least (Grade 1) with the worst (Grade 3) resistance state, the odds ratio was 7.4 (2.4-23) and the hazard ratio 6.7 (3.0-15). Associations were robust to unmeasured confounding, with E-values of 3-13. Grade 3 resistance showed the highest PAI-1/tPA and a2AP/plasminogen ratios. Ex vivo supplementation with plasminogen or a2AP iAb reversed fibrinolysis resistance from Grade 3 to Grade 1. Modelling these effects yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of 18-21% across Grades 2 and 3, and 32-36% in Grade 3. Conclusions. Fibrinolysis resistance measured at the bedside in sepsis reflects mechanistically reversible changes in fibrinolytic balance ex vivo. Modelling reversal by plasminogen supplementation or a2AP inhibition yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of up to 32% in the most severe resistance state. These hypothesis-generating estimates identify candidate interventions and provide a rationale for a clinical trial.

items.title_en: Prevalence and determinants of problematic khat use in Ethiopia
items.abstract_en: **Background** Evidence on khat use prevalence is substantial in Ethiopia and elsewhere. However, problematic khat use remains largely understudied because the concept has not been clearly defined or consistently measured. This study estimated the prevalence and determinants of problematic khat use among Ethiopian adults. **Methods** This descriptive cross-sectional analysis used baseline data from a prospective khat cohort study conducted in Butajira and adjacent districts in Central Ethiopia Regional State. We included 504 khat users who had chewed khat within the previous five years. Problematic khat use was assessed using the locally developed and validated 17-item Problematic Khat Use Screening Tool (PKUST-17). A score of >17 indicated problematic use. Binary and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors. **Results** Among the 504 khat users, most were male (82.3%), married (85.0%), and rural residents (70.8%). The prevalence of problematic khat use was 19.6%. Daily or near-daily khat users had eightfold higher odds of problematic use than occasional users (AOR = 8.05, 95% CI: 3.75-17.24). Stressful life events were associated with 3.48-fold higher odds of problematic use (AOR = 3.48, 95% CI: 1.56-7.76), while depressive symptoms were associated with 3.70-fold higher odds (AOR = 3.70, 95% CI: 2.00-6.75). **Conclusion** Problematic khat use affects approximately one in five khat users in Ethiopia. It is strongly associated with frequent khat use, stressful life events, and depressive symptoms. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal pathways and evaluate culturally appropriate prevention and treatment interventions.

items.title_en: Understanding widening socio-economic inequities in cardiovascular disease mortality in the Netherlands: A mixed methods protocol
items.abstract_en: Background: In the Netherlands, there is a substantial social gradient in mortality: individuals with higher socio-economic status are more likely to live longer lives than those with lower socio-economic status. There is evidence that this social gradient has widened since the mid-twentieth century, although why this has occurred is poorly understood. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) provides a particularly useful case study for understanding the mechanisms underlying this widening gradient. While CVD was historically the leading cause of death in the Netherlands, improvements in prevention and treatment have decreased CVD mortality, even as socio-economic inequalities in CVD mortality have increased. In this project, I aim to identify and test the mechanisms driving widening socio-economic inequities in CVD mortality over the last 75 years. Methods and analysis: This project uses mixed-methods. First, in participatory workshops, key stakeholders, e.g. policymakers, healthcare professionals, patient representatives, and individuals with lived experience of poverty, will co-create a conceptual model outlining the explanations linking socio-economic status and CVD in the Netherlands. Second, the conceptual model will provide the structure for the microsimulation, with the former defining which mechanisms will be represented in the latter. The microsimulation will maintain a common model structure across time, although population characteristics and individual trajectories will change to reflect successive twenty-year periods from the 1950s until today. The microsimulation will be validated by comparing simulated outcomes with historical data. Counterfactual scenarios will then be used to estimate the relative contribution of different mechanisms to the widening of socio-economic inequalities in CVD mortality. Ethics and dissemination: This project has been approved by the Social Sciences Research Ethics Committee of Wageningen University (approval number 2026-203). Participants will provide informed consent prior to participation. The microsimulation code will be made openly available, and findings will be disseminated through open-access publications, conference presentations, and a public summary co-designed with stakeholders.

items.title_en: MAScINSIGHT: A Real-World Data Study to Deepen Knowledge and Management of McCune-Albright Syndrome - Study Protocol for an Observational Study within OHDSI
items.abstract_en: Introduction McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is a rare congenital disorder affecting endocrine, skeletal and dermatological systems. MAS is often coded as fibrous dysplasia (FD) in routine health data, which includes other conditions and does not allow precise identification. This coding gap complicates reliable epidemiological estimates and clinical characterization. The study MAScINSIGHT aims to address this by investigating MAS features within FD-coded cohorts. Methods and analysis MAScINSIGHT is a retrospective observational study using a federated network of data in the OMOP Common Data Model. Routine data from multiple sites will be analyzed within a federated setting to assess endocrine abnormalities and treatment patterns in patients with FD or MAS. Ethics and dissemination Analyses will be performed locally at the data partner, with only aggregate statistics made available and centrally analyzed. The study protocol was approved by the ethics committee (reference number: 2026-18760-retrospektiv). Findings will be disseminated through open-access publications and patient-oriented reports.

items.title_en: Maternal Autoantibody Combinations as Predictors of Autism Risk: Retrospective Discovery and External Validation in a Prospective Cohort at Increased Risk
items.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Maternal Autoantibody-Related Autism (MARA) is a recently defined subset of autism characterized by specific combinations of maternal autoantibodies which cross the placenta and bind neurodevelopmentally critical target proteins. A clinical multi-ELISA MARA assay was recently rigorously analytically validated. The primary objective of this study was to assess the potential performance of this MARA autoantibody assay for predicting autism risk in high-risk populations. Secondary objectives were to establish the significant MARA autoantibody combinations and verify clinical discrimination in an external cohort. Methods: Bio-banked plasma samples from mothers of 420 autism and 335 typically developing (TD) children were analyzed by ELISA for MARA autoantibodies in combination. Transcendent autoantibody pairwise combinations were identified in discovery where both autoantibodies in a combination exceeded the values of every control participant. Permutation testing was used to establish that the probability of observed results significantly exceeded chance. Performance was then validated in an independent cohort (mothers of 42 autistic and 90 TD children). Results: Transcendent antibody levels were discovered in 70 mothers (16.7% of autism cases; no typically developing participants) in the discovery cohort. Specificity and positive predictive values for autism were 100% by construct. An external cohort showed similar performance with 14 (33.3%) transcendents. Permutation testing of each cohort demonstrated probabilities of transcendent cases to be significantly higher than expected be chance. Conclusions: The data reported here provides evidence for a high-risk subset of mothers of children with autism identified by the MARA autoantibody assay which enables further clinical validation.

items.title_en: A lifecourse perspective on sociodemographic intersectional inequalities in physical and mental health outcomes
items.abstract_en: Persistent inequalities in health outcomes continue to be a stubborn feature of many developed Western societies. To effectively understand health inequalities researchers must address two key criticisms: an overt focus on singular dimensions of disadvantage and a continuing need for longitudinal studies. Lifecourse intersectionality offers a framework to address these critiques through situating more nuanced and multidimensional understandings of the development of inequalities over time. We conduct a longitudinal Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA) examining both physical and mental health SF12 scores using UK Household Longitudinal Study data for adults (2009 to 2023). Forming intersections based on sex, ethnicity, generational cohort, education, and socioeconomic class, we identify a substantial degree of intersectional variation in our outcomes, and distinct differences in the development of intersectional inequalities in physical and mental health over the lifecourse. Intersectional inequalities are more pronounced for mental health compared to physical health, particularly at younger and older ages. In both cases, inequalities are additively patterned with generation and sex appearing most important to mental health and socioeconomic differences being stronger for physical health. However, our results also emphasise heterogeneity in the identified lifecourse intersectional effects, particularly in relation to how the patterning of the sociodemographic components for mental health vary by generational cohort. We therefore help reveal important complexity in the development of health inequalities in the UK and highlight the utility of longitudinal intersectional MAIHDA as a tool for quantitative intersectional researchers.

items.title_en: Motion-robust high-resolution 3D-GRASE pseudo-continuous ASL perfusion imaging at 3T
items.abstract_en: Purpose: High resolution arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based perfusion imaging is desirable for many applications but suffers from low SNR and motion sensitivity due to the necessity for highly segmented readouts. Acquisition and reconstruction strategies were optimized for motion-robust high-resolution pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) of the brain at 3T using segmented 3D Gradient and Spin Echo (3D-GRASE) at 2.0-mm isotropic resolution. Methods: A high-resolution 3D-GRASE pCASL sequence was implemented at 3T and evaluated with a focus on the interaction between background suppression strength and motion-corrected reconstruction, together with the fat suppression and control-tag subtraction strategies that strong suppression requires. Motion correction was performed using a novel motion-compensated (alignedSENSE-based) reconstruction that simultaneously estimates the motion and image, accounting for contrast changes between tag and control data. Eight healthy volunteers were scanned under motion-free and cued motion conditions. Image quality was assessed against motion-free reference images using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Results: The optimized acquisition-reconstruction pipeline enabled robust 2.0-mm isotropic pCASL at 3T and showed improved resistance to motion-related degradation. Strong BGS provided near-complete suppression of static tissue, and water excitation reduced lipid contamination and improved coil sensitivity estimation. The regularized alignedSENSE motion correction further improved perfusion-image quality, increasing SSIM by 18.7% under Strong BGS. Conclusion: Robust high-resolution pCASL at 3T can be achieved through combined optimization of acquisition and reconstruction. The combination of Strong BGS, water excitation, reference-superimposed processing, and regularized motion correction mitigates motion-related degradation and yields higher-quality perfusion images for high-resolution ASL.

items.title_en: Comparative efficacy and safety of targeted disease-modifying therapies in adults with primary IgA nephropathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
items.abstract_en: Background: Targeted disease-modifying therapies for adults with primary IgA nephropathy are increasing in number. However, head-to-head evidence is limited, and trial endpoints and follow-up durations vary. The relative effects of these therapies on short-term proteinuria control, long-term kidney outcomes, and safety remain unclear. Methods: We searched databases and trial registries for randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with a planned treatment duration of at least 24 weeks alongside stable or optimized supportive care. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses evaluated baseline-adjusted geometric mean ratios (GMRs) for 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 32 to 40 and 24 to 52 weeks, with Holm correction applied. Total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope and composite kidney outcomes were synthesized using common-effect models. Serious adverse events (SAEs) were analyzed using penalized-likelihood logistic regression within risk windows. Sensitivity analyses included restriction to evidence at low risk of bias, exclusion of interim or stage-specific reports, and assessment of precision-recovery assumptions and time-window boundaries. The Mantel to Haenszel method without continuity correction assessed the robustness of sparse SAE results. RoB 2 and CINeMA assessed risk of bias and evidence certainty, respectively. Results: Seventeen trials were included. At 32 to 40 weeks, telitacicept and subcutaneous sibeprenlimab had the lowest GMR point estimates versus placebo: 0.450 (nominal 95% CI 0.323 to 0.628) and 0.488 (0.355 to 0.671), respectively. None of the seven targeted treatment comparisons reached statistical significance after Holm correction. Iptacopan had the largest point estimate for improvement in annualized total eGFR slope: 3.020 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI 2.025 to 4.015). Composite kidney outcome hazard ratios were 0.570 (95% CI 0.401 to 0.811) for iptacopan and 0.440 (0.271 to 0.714) for targeted-release budesonide. Telitacicept had the lowest SAE odds ratio point estimate at 36 to 39 weeks: 0.314 (95% CI 0.105 to 0.938), although safety estimates were imprecise. In sensitivity analyses, proteinuria effect directions were generally consistent, but the 95% CIs for all retained comparisons included 1 after excluding interim or stage-specific reports; sparse SAE estimates remained imprecise. Evidence certainty was rated as low or very low. Conclusion: Although some regimens yielded the most favorable point estimates, the available evidence remains insufficient to establish treatment priorities or comparative safety advantages. Head-to-head trials are needed.

items.title_en: Distinct neural representations encode psychiatric states across timescales
items.abstract_en: Psychiatric states manifest over multiple timescales, from transient fluctuations in disorder-related distress to long-term variations in disease severity, yet whether these expressions share common neural representations remains unknown. We addressed this question in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) by comparing neural activity associated with momentary distress evoked by triggers versus that associated with clinically assessed chronic symptom severity. We analyzed intracranial recordings from the ventral capsule and orbitofrontal cortex spanning more than 4595 patient-days in 8 individuals undergoing deep brain stimulation therapy (NCT03457675, NCT04281134, NCT04806516), together with quantitative facial- and speech-derived behavioral measures. Neural signatures of OCD severity were dissociable from and stronger than signatures of momentary distress, indicating distinct underlying brain states. Integrating behavioral data into a predictive computational model improved neural decoding performance of both momentary distress and OCD severity. These findings show that acute manifestations of psychiatric illness are not simply short-timescale readouts of the same neural states that encode longer-term clinical burden. Instead, transient distress and longitudinal disease severity are represented by dissociable neural processes. This distinction has important implications for how psychiatric biomarkers and adaptive neuromodulation strategies should be designed.

items.title_en: Beyond reduced alpha power: a weaker temporal link between alpha and other brain rhythms in Alzheimer's disease
items.abstract_en: Background: Reduced alpha power is among the most consistently reported resting electroencephalography (EEG) features of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, alpha activity also interacts with other rhythms over time, a dynamic aspect that power measures do not capture. Whether AD weakens this temporal interaction, and whether such a change carries information beyond reduced alpha power, remains unclear. Methods: We analyzed public eyes-closed resting EEG from 29 healthy controls (HC), 36 patients with AD and 23 with frontotemporal dementia (FTD). After separating periodic from aperiodic activity, we tracked the aperiodic exponent and periodic theta, alpha, beta and gamma activity in consecutive 1-s windows. A vector autoregressive model predicted these five measures from the preceding window. Alpha's predictive contribution (G) was the increase in prediction error for theta, beta and gamma when the model was refitted without alpha as a predictor, with training and testing on separate time blocks of each recording. AD-HC differences were adjusted for age and sex, then for alpha expression (periodic alpha power) and signal quality (dynamic range and spatial reliability), with alpha self-persistence (alpha's carry-over between windows) as a benchmark. We also tested whether expression and G each added information about AD beyond the other. An exploratory Jansen-Rit-family circuit model examined whether expression and G can change partly independently. Results: G was lower in AD than in HC (adjusted difference in 10^3G, -3.19; 95% confidence interval -5.25 to -1.13; p = 0.0035), with a consistent direction across sensitivity analyses. Adjustment for alpha expression and signal quality retained 75.8% of this difference but only 4.4% of the self-persistence difference. Expression and G each added information beyond the other (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012 for both). FTD contrasts were inconclusive. In the circuit model, reducing local recurrent excitation lowered alpha expression without an estimated decrease in G, whereas reducing downstream input lowered G with a smaller change in expression. Conclusions: At the group level, the resting alpha abnormality in AD comprises two partly nonredundant dimensions: reduced expression and a weaker temporal link between alpha and subsequent multi-rhythm activity. Quantifying this temporal link may complement conventional spectral markers of AD.

items.title_en: A family-aware All of Us benchmark for polygenic prediction and genomic machine learning
items.title_zh: 面向多基因预测与基因组机器学习的家族感知All of Us基准
items.abstract_en: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have improved substantially in predictive performance, yet results remain difficult to compare across studies that differ in cohorts, phenotype definitions, and evaluation procedures. Comparison to machine-learning methods is harder still, since their performance depends strongly on how data are partitioned and whether related individuals leak across splits. Here, we introduce a family-aware benchmark for polygenic prediction built on version 9 of the All of Us Research Program (AoU). The benchmark assigns entire family components to fixed discovery, calibration, and test partitions, reserves first-degree relatives for within-family evaluation, and separates models trained only on AoU discovery data from those using external GWAS summary statistics. This enables direct comparison between conventional PRS pipelines and machine-learning models trained under identical data budgets. We report results for 14 binary disease traits. Our strongest scores explain 5.7-24.9% of liability-scale variance, with particularly strong prediction for Alzheimer's disease, type 2 diabetes, prostate cancer, glaucoma, and inflammatory bowel disease, and match or exceed published commercial and academic scores for most traits. Across 12 traits with interpretable within-family estimates of within-sibship-to-population effect ratio, 11 confidence intervals included a ratio of 1. Type 2 diabetes showed an attenuation ratio of 0.86 [0.76, 0.97].

items.title_en: Predicting Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Treatment Outcomes: A Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Topological Data Analysis Augmentation
items.abstract_en: We asked what topological structure adds to a clinical prediction model and how that addition should be measured. Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) treatment outcome prediction is the testbed. The contribution is an evaluation design and a bounded null result. Cross-sectional records for 9210 patients from the NIAID TB Portals programme were collated to one row per patient by worst-case aggregation, giving a 99-feature clinical schema. We derived two topological representations. A Mapper graph, built on a UMAP lens over a Gower dissimilarity, supplied four neighbourhood-position features. Local Vietoris--Rips persistent homology on each patient's 26-point neighbourhood supplied degree-0 and degree-1 summaries, vectorised by the best of thirteen catalogued methods. We compared five feature configurations across four classifiers in a pipeline in which every topological step is fitted inside the training partition. A sealed test lockbox of 1776 patients, 463 of them with adverse outcomes, was opened once. We compared discrimination by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) using paired DeLong tests with Bonferroni correction (corrected threshold 0.0125). No topologically augmented configuration meaningfully improved lockbox AUROC over the clinical-only baseline under any classifier. The best AUROC was 0.7548, achieved by the baseline with XGBoost. Across all sixteen comparisons the upper 95% confidence limit never exceeded +0.014 AUROC. Five comparisons met the corrected threshold. Four favoured the baseline, and one, under the support vector machine, favoured the augmented model by a negligible +0.0005 AUROC.The same features supported neighbourhood-based risk stratification and revealed variation in adverse-outcome composition across patient neighbourhoods: adverse-outcome purity ranged from 5.9% to 30.5% across the fifteen largest Mapper nodes, stably under resampling. The findings support a complementary framing of topological data analysis in clinical prediction. Topological features are best understood not as replacements for clinical predictors but as an analytical lens that reveals geometric structure in the patient population not captured by the clinical feature representation alone.

items.title_en: Fibrinolysis resistance in sepsis assessed by serial beside viscoelastometry is associated with plasma protein profiles and organ-failure severity: a prospective observational study
items.abstract_en: Background: Fibrinolysis resistance is associated with adverse outcomes in sepsis and can be quantified at the bedside by tissue plasminogen activator-enhanced viscoelastometric testing, using the fibrin-adjusted (FIBA10) clot lysis time (TPA-LT) expressed as the TPA-LT/FIBA10 ratio. In this study of adults admitted to intensive care with sepsis, plasma tissue plasminogen activator activity, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 activity (PAI-1), plasminogen and a2-antiplasmin were measured serially alongside TPA-LT/FIBA10 and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA-2) scores. Whether the bedside TPA-LT/FIBA10 measure of fibrinolysis resistance reflects the underlying plasma fibrinolytic protein environment, and whether it tracks organ-failure severity, has not been established. Results: This prospective observational study included 283 paired observations in 69 septic patients admitted with a median Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation III score 81, median SOFA-2 score 13 and a 38% ICU mortality. PAI-1 increased and plasminogen decreased with increasing fibrinolysis resistance (1.77 [1.50-2.09]-fold increase and 0.81 [0.76-0.87]-fold decrease, respectively, per e-fold increase in TPA-LT/FIBA10). Increasing organ-failure severity was also associated with increased PAI-1 and decreased plasminogen (1.23 [1.17-1.29]-fold increase and 0.95 [0.93-0.96]-fold decrease, respectively, per point increase in SOFA-2). In contrast, tissue plasminogen activator activity and absolute a2-antiplasmin did not relate to fibrinolysis resistance or organ failure. Principal component analysis of the fibrinolysis proteins, organ-failure severity and fibrinolysis resistance identified a dominant axis explaining 35% of the variance, on which PAI-1, SOFA-2 and TPA-LT/FIBA10 loaded together in opposition to plasminogen. Unsupervised clustering of the dataset, performed without reference to patient outcomes, separated a fibrinolysis inhibitor- high, substrate-depleted group with 61% mortality compared to 29% in the preserved- fibrinolysis group. During the ICU stay, PAI-1 decreased within 72 hours in survivors but remained unchanged in non-survivors (interaction p<0.001). A trend was observed for plasminogen levels increasing in survivors but remaining static in non-survivors. Conclusions: Changes in key fibrinolysis proteins, organ-failure severity and fibrinolysis resistance measured by viscoelastometry were coupled facets of the response to sepsis dominated by fibrinolysis inhibitor excess and substrate depletion rather than by reduced activator availability. These findings provide biological validation for bedside viscoelastometric quantification of fibrinolysis resistance and support prospective evaluation of substrate-directed profibrinolytic strategies.

items.title_en: Interventions for Cognitive Impairment in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Umbrella Review of Pharmacological and Lifestyle Strategies, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications
items.abstract_en: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the fastest-growing epidemics associated with cognitive impairment and dementia. This reduces quality of life among patients with diabetes. Several trials on the management of cognitive impairment have been conducted, although their effectiveness and mechanisms are still unclear. Aim: To synthesize evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs examining interventions for cognitive impairment in T2DM, stratified by intervention category, comparator, patient characteristics, mechanisms, and clinical outcomes. Methods: We identified 11 systematic reviews (n = 213,604 participants) reporting the effects of cognitive impairment interventions through a comprehensive literature search. Using random-effects models, a meta-meta-analysis was conducted and heterogeneity assessed using I{superscript 2} statistics. AMSTAR and GRADE were used to assess the quality of reviews. Subgroup analyses were conducted for intervention category, cognitive severity, age, diabetes duration, sex, and follow-up duration. Results: Sodium glucose co-transporter inhibitors showed the strongest cognitive improvement effect (pooled OR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.35-0.55; SUCRA = 94.5%), followed by GLP-1 receptor agonists (RR/OR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.50-0.72; SUCRA = 92.1%). Among lifestyle interventions, multi-component exercise was the most effective (SMD = 0.69-1.04). The lower baseline cognition (MMSE < 23) benefited more from GLP-1 receptor agonists (Cohen's d = -3.00, p < 0.001). Advanced age ([≥]60 years) and prolonged intervention time ([≥]24 weeks for medications; [≥]6 months for exercise) were associated with greater effects. Female gender showed greater benefit from GLP-1 receptor agonists (HR = 0.63 vs 0.81 for male gender). Conclusions: SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists have the greatest effect on cognition in T2DM, and multi-component exercise is the most effective lifestyle component. The review therefore recommends individualized selection of interventions based on patient characteristics and baseline cognitive status. This calls for high-quality trials with prolonged follow-up to strengthen the evidence base.

items.title_en: Association between Blood Lead Levels and Anaemia in a Pregnant Population in the Kintampo Area of Ghana: A Prospective Cohort Study
items.abstract_en: Background: Maternal anaemia and lead exposure both pose substantial risks in pregnancy, but their relationship has not been consistently explored. We assessed trimester-specific blood lead levels (BLLs) and their association with anaemia in pregnant women in the Kintampo area of Ghana. Methods: In this prospective cohort study nested within the PRISMA Maternal and Newborn Health Study in Ghana, 300 pregnant women were enrolled at <14 weeks' gestation and followed until delivery. Trimester-specific venous blood was collected and analysed for haemoglobin levels using Sysmex XN 330 auto analyser (Sysmex Corporation, Japan) and BLL using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Anaemia was defined as 11.0g/dL for first (T1) and third (T3) trimesters and 10.5g/dL for second (T2) trimester according to the World Health Organisation's (WHO's) trimester-specific haemoglobin thresholds and elevated BLL as [≥]3.5 {micro}g/dL by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Multiple logistic regression, adjusted for maternal age, parity, education, malaria parasitaemia, body mass index, gestational age and occupation, examined the BLL and anaemia association. A population-averaged Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) model was used to assess the association between elevated BLL and anaemia across trimesters. Results: The mean age of participants was 27.7{+/-}5.8 years (range 18-44years). Geometric mean BLL increased significantly across trimesters from 1.0 to 1.3 to 1.5 {micro}g/dL (p=0.003) for T1, T2 and T3 respectively. The prevalence of elevated BLL ([≥]3.5 {micro}g/dL) was 10.7%, 7.6%, and 15.2% for T1, T2, and T3 respectively. Anaemia prevalence increased significantly with increasing trimester from 34.7.0% to 59.3% to 76.0% (p<0.001) for T1, T2 and T3 respectively. In the population-averaged GEE model, elevated BLL was associated with increased odds of anaemia across trimesters, though this did not reach statistical significance (OR = 1.29, 95% CI: 0.77-2.17, p = 0.327). Conclusion: Anaemia prevalence in pregnancy is high in the Kintampo area and increases with advancing gestation. No significant association was observed between BLL and anaemia. These findings reinforce anaemia as a priority for urgent interventions in pregnancy through pathways independent of lead exposure. However, occupational lead surveillance and control remain important policy considerations.

items.title_en: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance
items.title_zh: 集体泵浦下Dicke超辐射的精确解析处理
items.abstract_en: We study the dynamics of an ensemble of $N$ two-level emitters undergoing collective decay at rate $Γ$ and collective incoherent pumping at rate $R$, confined to the fully symmetric Dicke ladder. Although the population dynamics are confined to a finite set of rate equations, their quantum-trajectory representation involves infinitely many pump-decay histories. We derive an exact finite continued fraction for the Laplace-transformed Dicke-state populations by resumming the infinitely many quantum trajectories generated by competing pump and decay processes. Our construction provides a physically transparent interpretation of the tridiagonal resolvent and extends to arbitrary permutationally symmetric initial states. In the strong- and weak-pumping regimes, we obtain perturbative transient solutions. We also identify exact relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables at balanced pump and decay strengths. Our solution provides a starting point for extending trajectory-based analytical methods to more general driven-dissipative collective systems.
items.abstract_zh: 我们研究 N 个二能级发射体的集合动力学：它们以速率 Γ 发生集体衰减、以速率 R 受到集体非相干泵浦，并被限制在完全对称的 Dicke 阶梯内。尽管布居动力学被约束在一组有限的速率方程中，其量子轨迹表示却涉及无穷多种泵浦-衰减历史。我们通过对竞争性泵浦与衰减过程所产生的无穷多条量子轨迹重新求和，为拉普拉斯变换后的 Dicke 态布居导出一个精确的有限连分式。我们的构造为三对角预解式提供了物理上透明的解释，并可推广至任意置换对称的初始态。在强泵浦与弱泵浦区间，我们得到微扰瞬态解；在泵浦与衰减强度平衡时，我们还确定了精确的弛豫本征值与辐射可观测量。该解为把基于轨迹的解析方法推广到更一般的驱动-耗散集体系统提供了起点。
items.highlight_zh: 用有限连分式精确求解集体泵浦Dicke超辐射的无穷轨迹。
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：Dicke 超辐射描述一群二能级原子集体发光时出现的增强辐射现象。若同时存在集体衰减和集体泵浦（把原子往上抽运），系统会表现出复杂的瞬态与稳态行为。这类问题看似简单：在完全对称的 Dicke 态阶梯上，布居演化只由有限个速率方程描述；但若用量子轨迹方法展开，就会遇到无穷多条“先泵浦、后衰减”的历史序列，难以解析求和。

方法：作者对这些无穷多条量子轨迹进行重求和，为拉普拉斯变换后的 Dicke 态布居推导出一个精确的有限连分式表达式。这一构造还揭示了三对角预解式的结构，并给出清晰的物理诠释；方法可推广到任意置换对称的初始态。

结果：在强泵浦与弱泵浦两个极限下得到微扰的瞬态解；在泵浦与衰减强度相等时，还精确求出了弛豫本征值和可观测的辐射量。

为何重要：它把一个看似需要无穷展开的集体耗散问题化为有限、精确且可计算的解析形式，为理解驱动-耗散型集体量子系统的瞬态动力学提供了基准解，也为将轨迹类解析方法推广到更一般的集体系统铺路，对量子光学与超辐射实验（如原子钟、激光）具有参考价值。

items.title_en: Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points
items.title_zh: Liouvillian 例外点处的最优量子分辨
items.abstract_en: Central to non-Hermitian sensing is the question of whether exceptional points (EPs) can make weak perturbations easier to detect. We show that despite enhanced spectral response, in finite-dimensional Lindblad systems with a unique stationary state and a nonzero relaxation gap, EPs offer no fundamental advantage in how the observation time required for reliable detection of a weak perturbation scales with the perturbation strength. We nevertheless demonstrate that by selectively choosing perturbations that enhance the quantum Fisher information rate, EPs can shorten the observation time needed to reach a predefined detection accuracy relative to a comparable non-EP reference at the same decay rate. As an illustration, we show using an optomechanical model at an EP that we can detect a weak force through the cavity output at the same reliability in less time than a non-EP reference. Our results establish fundamental limits on perturbation detection at EPs and can guide the design of faster non-Hermitian sensors based on optomechanical resonators, superconducting qubits, and trapped ions.
items.abstract_zh: 非厄米传感的核心问题是：例外点（EP）能否让弱扰动更容易被探测。我们证明，尽管谱响应增强，但在具有唯一稳态和非零弛豫间隙的有限维 Lindblad 系统中，EP 对可靠探测弱扰动所需观测时间随扰动强度变化的标度规律并无根本优势。不过我们也证明，若有针对性地选择能提高量子 Fisher 信息速率的扰动，EP 相比相同衰减率的非 EP 参照体系，可以缩短达到预定探测精度所需的观测时间。以处于 EP 的光机械模型为例，我们展示了通过腔输出可在更短时间内以相同可靠性探测弱力。本文结果确立了 EP 处扰动探测的基本极限，可指导基于光机械谐振器、超导量子比特和囚禁离子的更快非厄米传感器设计。
items.highlight_zh: EP 不改变探测时间标度律，但选对扰动可缩短观测时间
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究问题：例外点（EP）是非厄米系统中本征值和本征矢同时简并的特殊点，长期以来人们认为它能让微弱信号被放大、从而更容易探测。但此前讨论多基于无噪声的经典波动方程，在真正有噪声、有耗散的量子体系里，EP 是否仍有优势并不清楚。
2. 方法：作者在有限维 Lindblad 主方程框架下分析，假定系统有唯一稳态且存在非零弛豫间隙，考察“可靠探测一个弱扰动所需的观测时间”如何随扰动强度变小而增长，并与非 EP 的参照体系作对比；进一步用量子 Fisher 信息速率来刻画探测能力的提升，最后用一个处于 EP 的光机械模型做具体演示。
3. 结果：在标度意义下，EP 并不带来根本优势——所需观测时间的标度指数与非 EP 体系相同。但如果主动挑选那些能提升量子 Fisher 信息速率的扰动方向，EP 确实能在相同衰减率下比非 EP 参照更快达到同样的探测精度；光机械模型中，通过腔输出探测弱力所需时间确实更短。
4. 意义：这纠正了“EP 必然带来传感优势”的笼统印象，给出了基本极限，也指出可行的提速路径——不是靠 EP 本身，而是靠“选对扰动”和优化 Fisher 信息速率，对设计光机械、超导量子比特和离子阱类传感器有指导价值。

items.title_en: Mediated Interactions between Fermi Polarons in the Strongly Interacting Regime
items.title_zh: 强相互作用区费米极化子之间的媒介相互作用
items.abstract_en: Mediated interactions between quasiparticles lie at the heart of Landau Fermi-liquid theory, yet their behavior in the strongly correlated regime is not fully understood. Motivated by recent experiments [Nat. Phys. 20, 68--73 (2024)], we investigate mediated interactions between quasiparticles emerging from a Fermi sea---Fermi polarons---using zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo methods. Our main result is that the Landau interaction between polarons remains repulsive in the strongly interacting regime for any coupling strength in the polaronic branch, in contrast to the downward trend observed experimentally near resonance. Deep in the short-range universal regime, our results are insensitive to the microscopic details of the interaction potential, providing robust evidence for the sign of the ground-state induced interaction. In addition, we determine the real-space interaction between static impurities, recovering a Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY)-like behavior at weak coupling and the nonperturbative Born-Oppenheimer result at strong coupling. More broadly, our results establish a microscopic benchmark for how Landau quasiparticle interactions survive beyond the perturbative regime of strongly correlated quantum matter.
items.abstract_zh: 准粒子之间的媒介相互作用是朗道费米液体理论的核心，但其在强关联区域的行为尚未被完全理解。受近期实验 [Nat. Phys. 20, 68–73 (2024)] 启发，我们用零温量子蒙特卡罗方法研究由费米海涌现出的准粒子——费米极化子——之间的媒介相互作用。主要结果是：在极化子分支上，无论耦合强度如何，极化子之间的朗道相互作用在强相互作用区始终保持排斥，这与实验在共振附近观察到的下降趋势相反。在短程普适区深处，结果对相互作用势的微观细节不敏感，为基态诱导相互作用的符号提供了有力证据。此外，我们确定了静态杂质之间的实空间相互作用，在弱耦合下重现类 RKKY 行为，在强耦合下重现非微扰的 Born-Oppenheimer 结果。本文结果为强关联量子物质中朗道准粒子相互作用如何超越微扰区提供了微观基准。
items.highlight_zh: 强相互作用下极化子间的朗道相互作用始终为排斥
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究问题：在费米海中掺入少量杂质会形成“费米极化子”这种准粒子，它们之间会通过费米海产生间接的媒介相互作用。朗道费米液体理论预言这种相互作用，但强关联区域（如 Feshbach 共振附近）它是否还成立、是吸引还是排斥，此前并不清楚；近期有实验观察到共振附近吸引趋势增强，引发争议。
2. 方法：作者采用零温量子蒙特卡罗方法，直接数值求解强相互作用下杂质与费米海的耦合问题，计算极化子之间的朗道相互作用参数，并检验结果对具体相互作用势形式的依赖程度；同时计算两个静态杂质之间的实空间相互作用作为对照。
3. 结果：在整条极化子分支上，无论耦合多强，朗道相互作用始终保持排斥，并没有出现实验所暗示的下降/转吸引趋势；在短程普适区，结果几乎不依赖势的微观细节，说明结论稳健；实空间相互作用在弱耦合时表现为类 RKKY 振荡，在强耦合时吻合非微扰的 Born-Oppenheimer 描述。
4. 意义：这为强关联条件下朗道准粒子图像的有效范围提供了可靠的微观基准，也提示实验与理论之间仍需进一步沟通；对理解冷原子混合气体、以及更一般的强关联量子物质中的准粒子相互作用具有基础意义。

items.title_en: Classical Verification of Quantum Computation Beyond the Polynomial Hierarchy
items.title_zh: 超越多项式层级的量子计算经典验证
items.abstract_en: It is not known whether a classical polynomial-time verifier can verify arbitrary polynomial-time quantum computations with an efficient quantum honest prover without computational assumptions. We show that, relative to a classical oracle, such verification is possible for a language beyond the polynomial hierarchy that is decided exactly in quantum polynomial time. The protocol is public-coin, with perfect completeness and soundness error at most 1/4. To our knowledge, no language with such a proof system was previously proved to lie outside AM relative to an oracle. For every unbounded polynomial-time computable function, the oracle can be chosen so that the message count and the oracle query counts of the quantum algorithm, verifier, and honest prover are bounded by this function of the input length. The message count is optimal up to a constant factor, since for a suitable oracle every interactive proof system for the language uses at least a constant fraction of the messages of our protocol on infinitely many lengths, with a constant depending on its verifier. The language is a variant of recursive Fourier sampling in which code tables encode secrets that address data tables. The tables are evaluated recursively, and the oracle stores only the leaves. The quantum algorithm recovers every secret exactly, and the verifier checks the prover's secrets recursively against random code entries. The recursion restricts the input in a correlated way, as the same secret fixes the code bits and chooses the free coordinate, so Håstad's switching lemma does not apply. We prove a switching theorem for these restrictions, which may be of independent interest. For instances of sufficient height, no constant-depth circuit of size $2^{\mathrm{poly}(n)}$ changes its output with probability above $2^{-Ω(n)}$ when the answer of a random instance is flipped by changing a single leaf.

items.title_en: Catastrophes in Reconnections of Optical Vortex Rings
items.title_zh: 光学涡环重联中的灾变
items.abstract_en: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. Parameters that cause such striking outcomes are at the focal point of catastrophe theory - a branch of bifurcation theory that studies degenerate critical points of a potential function. We present theoretical study of topological configurations of optical vortex rings in elliptic Gaussian beams, which change dramatically at specific beam parameters. We identify two types of catastrophes, cusp and butterfly, near which very small changes of elliptic deformations lead to complex topological transformations of vortex rings.

items.title_en: Surface-Illuminated Interdigitated Ge-on-Si Avalanche Photodiode With Separated Ge Absorption, Si Multiplication, and Lateral Field Engineering
items.title_zh: 表面照射叉指型Ge-on-Si雪崩光电二极管，具有分离的Ge吸收、Si倍增和横向场工程
items.abstract_en: This work presents a surface-illuminated lateral Ge-on-Si interdigitated separate-absorption-charge-multiplication (SACM) avalanche photodiode for 1550-nm detection. The intrinsic-region spacing, P$^-$ charge-control width, and finger geometry are engineered to suppress high-field penetration toward the Ge/Si heterointerface and localize avalanche multiplication in Si. Simulations show that wider charge-control or intrinsic regions reduce fixed-bias dark current and shift avalanche onset to higher reverse bias. Among the tested structures, the intrinsic-region spacing/P$^-$ charge-control width of 0.5/0.15 $μ$m achieved a peak responsivity of 11.81 A/W at 1550 nm. At a -20 V applied voltage, it exhibited a multiplication gain of 3.796, a 3-dB bandwidth of 7.13 GHz, and a matched-bias gain-bandwidth product of 27.07 GHz. Optical-power-dependent measurements also show avalanche-gain compression consistent with space-charge screening. These results demonstrate effective lateral-field engineering for high-speed, surface-illuminated Ge-on-Si APDs.

items.title_en: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
items.title_zh: 动力学量子模拟作为量子信息的实验室
items.abstract_en: Dynamical quantum simulations are commonly designed to access a particular response function or correlation function. Yet the underlying protocol prepares a family of many-body states that contains information well beyond the observable for which the simulation was originally designed. In this work, we explore the idea of using these states as laboratories for quantum information. As a case study, we consider the local-pulse protocols used to compute Green functions in finite XX and XXX spin chains, and we interpret opposite source rotations as encoding a classical bit into the many-body system. This allows us to follow how the resulting record propagates, how it is encoded across local subsystems, and how readily it can be accessed with different measurements. We also find a clear separation between representation and readout. While fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed response in the XX chain, simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of the locally available information in the XXX chain. This reversed ordering persists when we move from finite-pulse discrimination to local source-angle estimation. Going beyond the source record, the same reduced states also allow us to reinterpret results in terms of Bell state recovery and quantum communication rates, as well as providing direct access to the evolving bipartite and genuine multipartite entanglement of the system. Our results show that dynamical quantum simulations developed for response calculations can naturally be used to ask a much broader set of quantum-information questions about the many-body states they already prepare.

items.title_en: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the $[\mathrm{CNOT}]$ Class with Fibonacci Anyons
items.title_zh: 基于Fibonacci任意子的[CNOT]类中间相遇编译
items.abstract_en: Compilation of two-qubit Fibonacci anyon gates is complicated by leakage ($\ell$) from the four-dimensional computational sector to the fifth state of the fusion space. We construct a GPU pipeline to find low-leakage representatives of the $[\text{CNOT}]$ class on different subsets of the braid group. We exhaustively explore the full positive five-generator alphabet up to $L=21$ with minimal leakage $\ell\sim10^{-3}$ and error $d_{[\text{CNOT}]}\sim 10^{-8}$ on it. To reach larger lengths, the search space is successively narrowed to three-generator, boundary-$σ_3$, and palindromic braids, and by considering only the Garside left normal form. These optimizations allow us to reach $L=72$. For $L=69$, a braid with $\ell\sim10^{-10}$ and $d_{[\text{CNOT}]}\sim 10^{-10}$ is found. In addition to directly enumerating optimal braids, we proved that $\ell\in\mathbb Z[\varphi]$, and any nonzero leakage obeys an exponential lower bound in the braid length, and obtained the limit laws $F_{3,\infty}(\ell)=\ell^2$ and $F_{5,\infty}(\ell)=\ell^4$ for our sets. Using asymptotics for the distribution function $F$, we showed that for sufficiently long braids, the asymptotics of exhaustive search are better than the asymptotics of random sampling for finding low-leakage braids.

items.title_en: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.title_zh: 在商用 CMOS 工艺后道工序集成两端铁电氧化铪突触权重
items.abstract_en: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.
items.abstract_zh: 在后道工序（BEOL）中用新兴材料实现功能化，是通往神经网络加速器和神经形态系统的重要路径。本文首次在出厂即用的商用 180 nm CMOS 芯片的后道工序中，实现了两端铁电突触权重的集成。作者提出一种新材料栈：将 WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] 双层结构夹在 TiN 与 Mo 电极之间。对于 450 °C 退火的器件，可在低于 1.8 V 下编程，循环间波动低于 3%。500 °C 退火的突触权重呈现更渐进的权重更新，而所测试的下层 NMOS 晶体管在完整集成流程后仍保持功能。作者通过硬件感知的神经网络仿真，说明了热预算与片上训练性能之间的权衡。
items.highlight_zh: 首次在商用 180 nm CMOS 后道集成两端铁电突触器件
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究问题：类脑计算与神经网络加速器希望把忆阻/铁电类“突触”器件直接做在芯片的金属互连层（后道工序 BEOL）里，与标准 CMOS 电路共集成。难点在于后道工序温度受限（一般不超过约 400–450 °C），而铁电氧化铪材料的结晶通常需要更高温，二者存在矛盾。
2. 方法：作者直接在采购来的商用 180 nm CMOS 裸片上做后道集成，提出 TiN / WOx-[HfO2-ZrO2] 双层 / Mo 的器件栈，用氧化钨层与氧化铪-氧化锆铁电层组合形成两端突触器件；分别在 450 °C 和 500 °C 退火，测量编程电压、循环间波动以及权重更新的线性度，并检查底层 NMOS 晶体管是否被后道工艺破坏。
3. 结果：450 °C 退火器件可在 1.8 V 以下编程，循环间波动小于 3%，适合做较陡的开关；500 °C 退火器件权重更新更渐进，更适合模拟型训练，但热预算更高。完整集成后底层 NMOS 仍能正常工作，说明工艺与商用 CMOS 兼容。作者进一步用硬件感知的神经网络仿真量化了“热预算—片上训练性能”的折中。
4. 意义：这是首次在现成商用 CMOS 的后道工序中集成两端铁电突触权重，为把神经形态功能以低成本、可量产的方式叠加到成熟工艺节点上提供了可行路径，也给出了工艺温度与训练性能之间如何取舍的实用参考。

items.title_en: Recovering classical gauge geometry from quantum master constraints
items.title_zh: 从量子主约束恢复经典规范几何
items.abstract_en: Exact normalizable solutions of quantum constraints form a symplectic submanifold of the space of rays, whereas classical first-class constraints define a surface on which the symplectic form is degenerate. We ask how the degenerate directions can be recovered when quantum theory is regarded as fundamental and the constraints are imposed through a single positive master operator. For a nonnegative master function whose zero set is a Morse--Bott critical manifold, the image of the linearized Hamiltonian vector field is the symplectic orthogonal of the zero set, and coisotropy is equivalent to this linearization having square zero. The image is fixed by the zero set, but the theorem identifies it with the response of the master dynamics, which makes it accessible to quantum states. Three realizations follow. The exact quantum physical space is the opposite, rotational case of the same dichotomy. For quadratic masters, the bottom of the spectrum is $(\hbar/2)\Tr_+L$, so first-class zero sets carry no offset of order $\hbar$; within the harmonic approximation this explains the $\hbar$ versus $\hbar^2$ offsets observed in tests of the master-constraint programme. Finally, the second time derivative of the limiting covariance of a semiclassical packet, which can be determined by bounded probes, has the gauge distribution as its image. Two oscillators at fixed total energy give exact master evolution, an exact realization of this covariance shear, and the reduced symplectic limit. For the non-Abelian SL(2,$\R$) model we compute the coherent and Weyl master symbols, prove essential self-adjointness and a finite-time propagation estimate, and derive the spectral bottom $\hbar^2/2$.

items.title_en: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
items.title_zh: 自适应信息挖掘：逼近超分辨成像的量子极限
items.abstract_en: The "Rayleigh limit" is not an intrinsic property of light, but a consequence of sub-optimal measurement of collected photons by the imaging instrument. To overcome this limitation, we present Adaptive Information Mining, a framework that achieves super-resolution by using sequentially refined measurements for incoming photons. Our approach employs a reconfigurable imaging system that dynamically reshapes the instrument measurement responses to maximize the Fisher information and guide scene estimation toward the fundamental quantum limit, even in deep sub-Rayleigh regimes. We demonstrate that this approach achieves an estimation error 2-5 times closer to the fundamental quantum limit than traditional direct imaging when imaging point sources, without requiring any prior knowledge of their positions and brightnesses. Importantly, we demonstrate that AIM can be extended to fully blind multi-parameter estimation in scenarios involving an unknown number of sources or turbulence-induced wavefront distortions. Our approach addresses the limitations of conventional fixed imaging, offering a practical path toward quantum-limited super-resolution imaging.

items.title_en: Homodyne Unravelling and Parameter Estimation in Squeezed Thermal Baths
items.title_zh: 压缩热浴中的零差解缠与参数估计
items.abstract_en: We derive an alternative formulation of the stochastic master equation describing the evolution of quantum systems continuously measured via homodyne detection in a squeezed-thermal environment. This formulation allows us to identify two distinct collapse operators, corresponding respectively to the monitored and unmonitored channels, and to express the quantum state evolution directly in terms of Kraus-like operators. As a consequence, it facilitates the application of advanced numerical methods that account for higher-order corrections and discrete-time monitoring, and it also enables the efficient numerical evaluation of Cramér-Rao bounds in parameter estimation problems. To demonstrate the latter, we evaluate the Fisher information of the continuous homodyne monitoring for qubit frequency estimation in the presence of a squeezed-thermal bath. Our results show that exponential scaling of the steady-state Fisher information rate with squeezing is retained even at non-zero temperature.

items.title_en: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams
items.title_zh: 自由电子束中的库仑结晶
items.abstract_en: Classical Coulomb crystals and quantum Wigner crystals typically arise when repulsive interactions order like-charged particles in spatially confined environments. Here, we show that transient crystallization can also emerge in freely propagating electron pulses without external trapping. Experimentally, we use a transmission electron microscope to measure number-resolved energy correlations in photoemitted pulses containing up to nine electrons, revealing strong correlations at small particle numbers that progressively disappear in the pulse interior as the number increases. To explain these observations, we combine many-body simulations with a one-dimensional statistical-mechanical model, showing that the leading and trailing electrons generate a self-induced longitudinal potential that transiently confines the inner particles, enabling the formation of an ordered chain during propagation. The resulting crystallization phase diagram reveals how many-body ordering dynamics can be understood in terms of evolving macroscopic beam properties, namely its geometry and the ratio of the mean Coulomb interaction energy to the longitudinal thermal energy. Extending this framework, we theoretically demonstrate that weak transverse guiding through electrostatic or optical ponderomotive forces can sustain crystallization at larger particle numbers and predict spontaneous longitudinal periodic bunching in continuous electron beams.
